Press a card to open the listing, group, opportunity or event. On a card you can also:

- press **Message** to write to the member who posted a listing;
- press **Save match** to keep a listing match;
- press **Not interested** and choose a reason, so you see fewer matches like it;
- press **Join** on a group match.

## Event matches

Event matches are upcoming events that you have not replied to yet. They are shown under **All**, marked **Event**. Open the event to see the details and say if you are going.

## Getting better matches

Listing matches are based on your own listings. If you have none, the page asks you to **Create a listing**. Group, volunteering and event matches also use the categories of your listings and the skills and bio on your profile. Adding a location to your profile helps with distance.

match_preferences.title: Changing your match preferences
match_preferences.summary: Pause matching, set distance and quality, and choose how often you hear about matches.
match_preferences.body:
You can control how matching works for you.

1. Open [Matches](/matches) and press **Match preferences**.
2. Change the settings you want.
3. Press **Save preferences**.

The settings are:

- **Pause matching**: stops new suggestions and notifications until you turn it off again.
- **Maximum distance** and **Minimum match quality**, under **Distance & quality**.
- **Category interests**: tick the categories you want matches for. Leave them all unticked to match on every category.
- **Match digest frequency**: **Daily**, **Fortnightly**, **Monthly** or **Never**.
- **Hot match alerts**: be told straight away about very strong matches.
- **Mutual match alerts**: be told when a match works both ways.

Distance settings only work if your profile has a location.

skills_and_endorsements.title: Skills directory and endorsements
skills_and_endorsements.summary: Browse the skills members share, add your own, and endorse other members.
skills_and_endorsements.body:
The **Skills** page shows the skills members share, grouped by category.

1. Open [Skills](/skills).
2. Search for a skill, or open a category.
3. Choose a skill to see members who offer it (**Offers**) and members who want it (**Wants**).

## Adding your own skills

1. On the Skills page, press **Add your own skills**. This opens the **Skills** tab in your settings.
2. Press **Add Skill**.
3. Choose a skill and your level, such as **Beginner** or **Expert**.

## Endorsing someone

An endorsement is a quick way to say a member is good at a skill.

1. Open the member's profile.
2. Next to one of their skills, press the small endorse button. It says "Endorse" followed by the skill when you point at it.

Press it again to remove your endorsement. The number beside a skill shows how many members have endorsed it.

messages.title: Messages
messages.summary: Write privately to other members, send voice notes and understand safety notices.

start_conversation.title: Sending a private message
start_conversation.summary: Start a one-to-one conversation with another member.
start_conversation.body:
Messages are private conversations between you and one other member.

## Start a conversation

- From a profile: press **Send Message**.
- From the Messages page: open [Messages](/messages), press **New Message**, search for the member and choose them.
- From a listing: press **Send Message**, if your community shows it. The conversation then shows which offer or request it is about.

## Write and send

Type in **Type a message...** and press Enter, or press the send button. To start a new line, hold Shift and press Enter. A message can be up to 10,000 characters.

Your conversations are listed in the **Inbox** tab. Use **Search conversations...** to find one. Inside a conversation, the magnifier button searches its messages.

> If you see **Direct Messaging Disabled**, your community has turned off private messages. Use exchange requests instead. If you see **Messaging Restricted**, a community administrator has limited your messaging. Contact your coordinator if you think this is a mistake.

voice_and_attachments.title: Voice messages and attachments
voice_and_attachments.summary: Record a voice message or attach a picture or document.
voice_and_attachments.body:
You can send a recorded voice message or attach a file.

## Voice message

1. In a conversation, press the microphone button.
2. If your browser asks, allow it to use your microphone.
3. Speak. The screen shows **Recording...**.
4. Press **Stop** when you finish.
5. Listen back if you like. Press **Send**, or **Cancel** to throw it away.

If you see **Microphone Access Required**, allow the microphone in your browser settings and try again.

## Attachments

1. Press the paperclip button. On a phone, you may need to press the arrow first to show it.
2. Choose a file. You can attach pictures, PDF files, Word documents and text files.
3. Add a message if you like, then send.

To remove a file before you send it, press the cross next to it.

You can also react to a message with an emoji.

edit_delete_messages.title: Editing and deleting your messages
edit_delete_messages.summary: Change a message you sent, or remove it for you or for both of you.
edit_delete_messages.body:
You can change or remove messages you have sent.

## Edit a message

1. Point at your message, or press and hold it on a phone, and open the message options.
2. Choose **Edit**.
3. Change the text and press **Save**.

You can edit a message for up to 24 hours after you send it. An edited message shows **(edited)**. Voice messages cannot be edited.

## Delete a message

1. Open the message options and choose **Delete**.
2. Choose one of these:

- **Delete for everyone** removes the text for both of you. It is replaced by **[Message deleted]**.
- **Delete for me** hides it from your view only. The other member still sees it.

Press **Cancel** if you change your mind.

> Think before you send. The other person may read a message before you edit or delete it.

archive_delete_conversations.title: Removing or restoring a conversation
archive_delete_conversations.summary: Move a conversation out of your inbox, remove it for both of you, or bring it back.
archive_delete_conversations.body:
You can clear a conversation out of your inbox.

1. Open the conversation.
2. Press the **More options** button (three dots) at the top.
3. Choose **Delete for me** or **Delete for everyone**.
4. Press **Delete** to confirm.

**Delete for me** moves the conversation to your **Archived** tab. The other member keeps their copy.

**Delete for everyone** removes the conversation from both your inbox and theirs.

## Restoring a conversation

1. Open [Messages](/messages) and choose the **Archived** tab.
2. Press **Restore** next to the conversation.

It moves back to your **Inbox**.

If the other member writes to you again, the new messages appear in your inbox as usual.

message_translation.title: Translating messages
message_translation.summary: Read messages in your own language, one at a time or for a whole conversation.
message_translation.body:
If your community uses message translation, you and the other member can each write in your own language.

## Translate one message

Under a message, press **Translate to** followed by your language. The translation appears with a **Translated** label.

Press **View original** to see the words that were sent. Press **Show translation** to switch back.

## Translate a whole conversation

Press the translate button at the top of the conversation. On a phone, open **More options** (three dots) and choose **Translate messages automatically**.

A note says messages are being translated into your language. Press **Turn off** to stop.

The language used is the one you have chosen for this website.

> Translations are made automatically by a computer. They can be wrong, especially for names, slang or local words. If something matters, check with the other person.

coordinator_review_notice.title: Why does it say a coordinator may review messages?
coordinator_review_notice.summary: What the safeguarding notice in a conversation means, and why it looks the same for everyone.
coordinator_review_notice.body:
Some conversations show this notice: "Messages in this conversation may be reviewed by a coordinator for safeguarding, or visible to someone a participant trusts to support them." On a phone, it appears as **Safeguarded conversation**.

It means one or both of these may be true:

- A community coordinator may read the messages to help keep members safe.
- One of you has chosen a supporter, such as a family member or carer, who can view their messages.

The notice is worded the same way whatever the reason. This protects the privacy of anyone who has a supporter.

You can close the notice with the cross. It comes back when you open the conversation again.

If you have chosen a supporter yourself, you will also see "Someone you chose as a supporter can view your messages." Press **Manage this** to change it.

> Write as you would in a shared space. Never send passwords or bank details in a message.

coordinator_arrangement_needed.title: Coordinator arrangement needed
coordinator_arrangement_needed.summary: What to do when you cannot message a member directly because of safeguarding settings.
coordinator_arrangement_needed.body:
Sometimes you cannot message a member directly. A red box appears at the top of the conversation, and you cannot send messages there.

## Coordinator arrangement needed

This member's safeguarding preferences say contact must be arranged by a coordinator. It is not a judgement about you.

1. Press **Request coordinator help**.
2. A note confirms the coordinator has been told.
3. A broker, administrator or coordinator will contact you to help arrange things.

## Community confirmation needed

Your community needs to confirm a safety check (sometimes called vetting) before you can contact some members. Press **Request review of my vetting** to ask a broker to look at your record. Do not send certificates or criminal-record details through messages.

## You can contact coordinators and vetted members

If you told your community you consider yourself a vulnerable adult, you can contact coordinators and members whose vetting your community has recorded. This is to keep you safe. Ask a coordinator if you would like help getting in touch with someone else.

## Safeguarding check temporarily unavailable

The safety rules could not be checked at the moment, so messaging is paused. Wait a little and press **Check again**. If it keeps happening, ask a coordinator.

blocking_members.title: Blocking a member
blocking_members.summary: Stop a member from contacting you, and unblock them later if you wish.
blocking_members.body:
Blocking stops a member from contacting you.

## Block someone

1. Open their profile.
2. Press the **More options** button (three dots).
3. Choose **Block User**.
4. Press **Block User** again to confirm.

A blocked member cannot see your profile, message you or interact with your content. Their profile then shows "You have blocked this user".

## Unblock someone

1. Open [Blocked Users](/settings/blocked). You can also reach it from the **Privacy** tab in your settings.
2. Press **Unblock** next to their name and confirm.

You can also press **Unblock User** on their profile.

After you unblock someone, they can see your profile and message you again. You are not reconnected automatically.

> If someone makes you feel unsafe, tell your coordinator as well as blocking them.

exchanges.title: Exchanges
exchanges.summary: Request help, agree the hours and confirm the time once the work is done.

how_exchanges_work.title: How does an exchange work?
how_exchanges_work.summary: The steps from a first request to the hours moving between wallets.
how_exchanges_work.body:
An exchange is how two members agree on help and record the hours. Everything is kept in one place, from the request to the final hours.

1. **Request**: you open a listing, press **Request Exchange** and propose the hours.
2. **Answer**: the member who posted the listing accepts or declines.
3. **Approval**: if your community requires it, a broker checks the exchange. A broker is a community coordinator who helps arrange exchanges.
4. **Start**: the member who posted the listing presses **Start Exchange** when the work begins.
5. **Finish**: they press **Mark Complete** when it is done.
6. **Confirm**: both of you confirm the hours worked.
7. **Payment**: when the confirmations agree, the hours move from the person who received help to the person who gave it.

You can follow all your exchanges on [My Exchanges](/exchanges). Each exchange page has an **Exchange Timeline** showing every step.

> The member who posted the listing always does the accept, start and mark complete steps, even when their listing is a request for help. On the exchange page they are shown as the **Provider**, and the person who sent the request as the **Requester**.

request_exchange.title: Requesting an exchange from a listing
request_exchange.summary: Send a request with your proposed hours and a message.
request_exchange.body:
1. Open the listing you are interested in.
2. Press **Request Exchange**.
3. Check **Proposed Hours**. It starts at the listing's estimate. Change it if you have agreed something different.
4. Add a **Message (optional)** to explain what you need or ask a question.
5. Press **Send Request**.

The exchange page opens. Its status shows **Awaiting Provider** until the other member answers. They get a notification about your request.

If you see **Broker Approval Required**, a coordinator must also approve the exchange before it can go ahead.

After sending, check the hours shown on the exchange page. If they are not what you expected, cancel and send a new request.

You cannot request an exchange on your own listing. If you already have an open exchange for a listing, the listing shows **Exchange** with its status instead of **Request Exchange**.

> A request can be refused because of your community's safety rules or the other member's settings. If your request fails and you are not sure why, contact your coordinator.

respond_to_request.title: Accepting or declining a request
respond_to_request.summary: What to do when someone asks for an exchange on your listing.
respond_to_request.body:
When someone requests an exchange on your listing, you get a notification. The request appears on [My Exchanges](/exchanges) with the label **Respond**.

1. Open the exchange.
2. Read the **Proposed Hours** and any **Message from requester**.
3. Press **Accept Request** to agree, or **Decline** to say no.

If you decline, you can add a **Reason (optional)**. Then press **Decline Request**. The other member is told.

After you accept, the status becomes **Accepted**. If your community needs broker approval, it shows **Awaiting Broker** first.

To talk about the details before you decide, press **Message** followed by the member's name, if your community has private messages.

> Only accept work you are able and willing to do. It is fine to decline.

start_and_complete.title: Starting and finishing the work
start_and_complete.summary: Tell the other member when the work begins and when it is done.
start_and_complete.body:
The member who posted the listing moves the exchange along.

1. When the work begins, open the exchange and press **Start Exchange**. The status becomes **In Progress**.
2. When the work is done, press **Mark Complete**. The status becomes **Confirm Hours**.

The other member gets a notification at each step.

Next, both of you confirm how many hours the work took. No hours move until you both confirm. See "Confirming the hours".

While the exchange is under way, you can keep in touch with the **Message** button on the exchange page.

Once the work has started, the exchange can no longer be cancelled from the exchange page. If plans change, talk to the other member or your coordinator.

confirm_hours.title: Confirming the hours
confirm_hours.summary: Both members confirm the time taken, then the hours move.
confirm_hours.body:
Once the work is marked complete, both of you confirm how long it took. Hours only move when both of you have confirmed.

1. Open the exchange. You can find it in the **Needs Confirmation** tab of [My Exchanges](/exchanges).
2. Press **Confirm Hours**.
3. Check the number in **Hours**. It starts at the proposed hours. Change it if the work took more or less time.
4. Press **Confirm Hours** in the box.

When you have both confirmed:

- If the two numbers match, or are within a quarter of an hour, the exchange completes. Close numbers are averaged.
- If they are further apart, the exchange is marked **Disputed** and a broker reviews it.

Your community may limit how far the confirmed hours can differ from the proposed hours. If you enter a number outside that range, the nearest allowed number is used.

When the exchange completes, the hours move from the person who received help to the person who gave it.

> If the person paying does not have enough hours, the exchange cannot complete. You will see a message, and no hours move.

broker_approval.title: What does broker approval mean?
broker_approval.summary: Why some exchanges wait for a coordinator, and what happens next.
broker_approval.body:
A broker is a community coordinator who helps arrange exchanges safely. Some communities ask a broker to approve exchanges before they go ahead.

You may see **Broker Approval Required** when you send a request. After the other member accepts, the status shows **Awaiting Broker**, and the timeline shows **Sent to Broker**.

The broker then either:

- approves the exchange, and the status becomes **Accepted**; or
- rejects it, and the exchange is cancelled.

Both of you are told either way. The broker may leave a note, shown under **Broker Notes** on the exchange page.

An exchange may need approval because of your community's settings, the number of hours, the kind of listing, or a member's safeguarding preferences. You do not need to do anything while you wait.

cancel_exchange.title: Cancelling an exchange
cancel_exchange.summary: Withdraw a request before the work starts.
cancel_exchange.body:
The member who sent the request can cancel an exchange before the work starts.

1. Open the exchange.
2. Press **Cancel Exchange**.
3. Press **Cancel Exchange** again to confirm, or **Keep Exchange** to go back.

You can cancel while the status is **Awaiting Provider**, **Awaiting Broker** or **Accepted**. The other member is told. No hours move.

> Cancelling cannot be undone. If you change your mind, send a new request.

If you posted the listing, you can **Decline** a request instead of accepting it.

Once the work has started, the cancel button is no longer shown. If plans change after that, talk to the other member or your coordinator.

exchange_disputes.title: What happens if we disagree about the hours?
exchange_disputes.summary: What happens when members confirm different hours, and what a coordinator can do in the Broker Panel.
exchange_disputes.body:
If you and the other member confirm hours that are too far apart, the exchange is marked **Disputed**. The page says "There is a disagreement about the hours. A broker will review this."

You both get an email about it. No hours move yet.

In the Broker Panel, a broker can:

- read the exchange history and speak to both members; and
- if hours should move, adjust each member's balance with a clear reason.

The Broker Panel has no button to settle or cancel a disputed exchange. Balance adjustments do not change the exchange's **Disputed** status. Ask your coordinator what was done.

To avoid a dispute, agree the hours with the other member before you both confirm.

To report another kind of problem, such as someone not turning up, press **Report a problem** on the exchange in the phone app. The website does not have this button; contact your coordinator there.

rate_exchange.title: Rating an exchange
rate_exchange.summary: Give a star rating and comment after an exchange is completed.
rate_exchange.body:
After an exchange is completed, you can rate how it went.

1. Open the completed exchange.
2. Press **Rate This Exchange**.
3. Choose one to five stars, from **Poor** to **Excellent**.
4. Add a **Comment (optional)**.
5. Press **Submit Rating**, or **Skip** to close without rating.

You can rate each exchange once. Ratings from both members appear under **Ratings** on the exchange page.

If your community uses reviews, you can also write a review that appears on the member's profile. See the Reviews section of this guide.

reviews.title: Reviews
reviews.summary: Leave feedback after an exchange and see what others say about you.

leave_review.title: How do I leave a review?
leave_review.summary: Rate a member after you have exchanged hours, or write a review from their profile.
leave_review.body:
A review is a star rating, with an optional comment, that appears on a member's profile.

## After an exchange

1. Open [Reviews](/reviews).
2. Choose the **Pending Reviews** tab. It lists people you have exchanged hours with and not yet reviewed.
3. Press **Write Review**.
4. Choose a **Rating** from one to five stars.
5. Add a **Comment (Optional)**, up to 2,000 characters.
6. Press **Submit Review**.

## From a profile

1. Open the member's profile.
2. Press **More options** (three dots) and choose **Write Review**.
3. Choose a rating, add a comment if you like, and press **Submit Review**.

A review linked to an exchange is marked **Transaction Review**. A review written from a profile is a **General Review**.

You can review each exchange once. You can write a general review of the same member once a day.

> Be fair and specific. Reviews help other members decide who to work with.

manage_reviews.title: Reading and managing your reviews
manage_reviews.summary: See reviews you have received and written, and delete one you wrote.
manage_reviews.body:
Open [Reviews](/reviews) to see three tabs:

- **Reviews Received**: what other members have said about you, with your **Average Rating** and **Total Reviews**.
- **Reviews Given**: the reviews you have written.
- **Pending Reviews**: exchanges you can still review.

## Deleting a review you wrote

1. Open the **Reviews Given** tab.
2. Press the delete button on the review.
3. Confirm.

You cannot delete reviews that other members wrote about you. If a review about you seems unfair or unsafe, contact your coordinator.

## Other members' reviews

A member's reviews appear on their profile, in the **Reviews** tab. Their listings also show their rating and how many reviews they have.

wallet.title: Wallet and hours
wallet.summary: Check your balance, send hours, donate and see your history.

wallet_overview.title: Your wallet at a glance
wallet_overview.summary: Where to see your balance, send hours and find your history.
wallet_overview.body:
Your wallet holds your time credits. One time credit is one hour.

Open [Wallet](/wallet) to see:

- **Your Balance**, in hours.
- Totals for **Earned**, **Spent** and **Pending**.
- The **Send Credits** and **Donate** buttons.
- The **Community Fund**, a shared pool of hours for your community.
- Your **Transaction History**.

You earn hours when you help someone and they pay you, through an exchange or a transfer. You spend hours when someone helps you.

Press **Refresh** to load the latest figures.

If you manage an organisation in your community, its hours are kept separately, in the organisation's own wallet on its dashboard.

send_hours.title: How do I send hours to someone?
send_hours.summary: Pay a member for time they gave you, straight from your wallet.
send_hours.body:
You send hours to pay a member for time they gave you.

1. Open [your wallet](/wallet).
2. Press **Send Credits**.
3. In **Search by name or username...**, type the member's name and choose them from the list.
4. Enter the **Amount (hours)**. You can use part-hours, such as 1.5.
5. If you like, choose a **Category** and add a **Description**, such as what the help was.
6. Check the summary. It shows who you are paying and your new balance.
7. Press **Send Credits**.

You will see **Transfer successful**. The hours appear in both wallets.

You can also press **Send Credits** on a member's profile. The form opens with that member already chosen.

You cannot send more hours than you have. Your community may also set a limit for a single transfer.

> Check the name and amount carefully before you send. You cannot cancel a transfer yourself. If you make a mistake, contact your coordinator.

transaction_history.title: Your transaction history
transaction_history.summary: See every payment in and out of your wallet, filter it and download it.
transaction_history.body:
**Transaction History** on [your wallet](/wallet) lists the hours that have come in and gone out.

Each entry shows a description, the other member and the amount. Hours you received show with a plus sign. Hours you sent show with a minus sign.

Use the tabs to filter the list: **All**, **Earned**, **Spent** or **Pending**.

Press **Load More** to see older entries.

Press **Export** to download your history as a spreadsheet file (CSV). It includes the date, type, amount, description, other member and status. Only the entries loaded on screen, in the tab you have chosen, are included. For your full history, choose **All**, press **Load More** until no older entries appear, then press **Export**.

## Group exchanges

When a group exchange is completed, each payment appears as its own entry, starting "Group exchange:" followed by the exchange title. You can see exactly who paid whom.

starting_balance.title: Do new members get a starting balance?
starting_balance.summary: Some communities give new members hours to start with. It is a community setting.
starting_balance.body:
Your community may give new members some hours to start with. This lets you ask for help before you have given any.

Whether there is a starting balance, and how many hours it is, is set by your community. When it applies, the hours are usually added when you join or when your account is approved. They appear in your [transaction history](/wallet).

If you expected a starting balance and cannot see one, contact your coordinator.

Your community's administrators can also add hours to members' wallets for other reasons.

insufficient_balance.title: What does "insufficient balance" mean?
insufficient_balance.summary: You do not have enough hours for what you are trying to do. Nothing has been taken.
insufficient_balance.body:
"Insufficient balance" means you do not have enough hours for what you are trying to do.

You may see it when you:

- send hours with **Send Credits** (the form shows **Exceeds available balance**);
- donate hours;
- confirm hours at the end of an exchange where you are the one paying;
- are a receiver in a group exchange when it is completed.

Nothing is taken from your wallet when this happens.

## What you can do

- Check **Your Balance** in [your wallet](/wallet).
- Send or agree a smaller number of hours.
- Earn hours by helping someone, for example by posting an offer.
- Ask your coordinator if you think your balance is wrong.

donate_hours.title: Donating or gifting hours
donate_hours.summary: Give hours to your community fund or to another member.
donate_hours.body:
You can give hours away without an exchange.

1. Open [your wallet](/wallet) and press **Donate**.
2. Under **Donate to**, choose **Community Fund** or **Another Member**.
3. If you chose **Another Member**, search for them under **Search by member** and choose them.
4. Enter the **Amount (hours)**. Your balance is shown under the box.
5. Add a **Message (optional)** if you like.
6. Press **Donate**.

You will see **Donation sent!**. Donations cannot be taken back.

## About the Community Fund

The **Community Fund** is a shared pool of hours for your community. The fund card on your wallet shows how many hours it holds. You can also press **Donate** on that card.

Your community's administrators decide how the fund is used. They can give hours from it to members.

hours_without_exchange_requests.title: Recording hours when there are no exchange requests
hours_without_exchange_requests.summary: If your community does not use exchange requests, pay for help from your wallet.
hours_without_exchange_requests.body:
Some communities do not use exchange requests. In that case, listings show **Send Message** instead of **Request Exchange**.

Here is how to record an exchange then:

1. Find a listing and press **Send Message** to agree the details, including the number of hours.
2. Do the exchange.
3. The person who received the help pays. They open [their wallet](/wallet), press **Send Credits**, choose the member, enter the hours and add a short description.

You can also send hours from the member's profile, with **Send Credits**.

> Only send hours for time that has been given. If something went wrong, talk to the other member or your coordinator before paying.

group_exchanges.title: Group exchanges
group_exchanges.summary: Record hours for activities where several people give or receive time.

what_is_group_exchange.title: What is a group exchange?
what_is_group_exchange.summary: One exchange that records time for several people at once.
what_is_group_exchange.body:
A group exchange records time when more than two people are involved. For example, a member runs a class for a group, or several neighbours help at a garden workday.

The basic rule is simple: one hour of time is one time credit. People giving time earn credits. People receiving time pay them.

When you add people, each one goes on one side:

- **Giving time**: the person gives their time and earns credits.
- **Receiving time**: the person receives time and pays credits.

The member who sets it up is the organiser. The organiser chooses the kind of group exchange, adds the people, starts the exchange and completes it. The organiser only earns or pays credits if they also add themselves.

There are five kinds, and the form explains each one: **Workshop or class**, **A team helping someone**, **Share equally**, **Share by amount of effort** and **Type each person's hours**. Before you create the exchange, the page shows **What everyone will earn or pay**, so you can see exactly what each person will earn or pay.

Everyone must confirm before any time credits move. When the organiser completes the exchange, everyone's balance changes together.

Open [Group Exchanges](/group-exchanges) to see yours. The tabs are **All**, **Active**, **Needs Confirmation**, **Completed** and **Cancelled**.

create_group_exchange.title: Creating a group exchange
create_group_exchange.summary: Set up a group exchange in four steps.
create_group_exchange.body:
The form has four steps: **Details**, **Participants**, **Review Split** and **Confirm**.

1. Open [Group Exchanges](/group-exchanges) and press **New Exchange**.
2. On **Details**, enter a **Title**. You can add a **Description (optional)** too. Under **What kind of group exchange is this?**, choose the kind that fits. **Workshop or class** is chosen to begin with. Then enter the hours the page asks for. Press **Next**.
3. On **Participants**, search for members by name. Press **Giving time** or **Receiving time** next to each person. You need at least one person on each side. Where the page asks for hours, check each person's hours and change any that are wrong. Press **Next**.
4. On **Review Split**, read **What everyone will earn or pay**. Check that it is what you expect. If something is wrong, a message tells you what to change. Press **Review**.
5. On **Confirm**, check everything and press **Create Group Exchange**.

The hours you enter depend on the kind. For a workshop, it is the length of the session. For a team, it is the hours each helper spent. The guide "The five kinds of group exchange" explains each kind.

The exchange is saved as a **Draft**. Nobody is asked to confirm yet. Before you start it, you can still add people with **Add Participants**, or remove them with the cross next to their name.

When you are ready, press **Start Exchange**. Everyone then confirms their hours, and you press **Complete Exchange**. The guide "Starting, confirming and completing a group exchange" has the details.

Type at least two letters to search. You can only find members who are listed in the member directory. Each member can be added once.

People added later with **Add Participants** have no hours set. If you use **Workshop or class**, **A team helping someone** or **Type each person's hours**, add everyone while you create the exchange.

> Your community's safety rules may stop some members from being added to a group exchange.

providers_receivers.title: Giving time, receiving time and adding yourself
providers_receivers.summary: Put each person on the right side, and add yourself if you are taking part.
providers_receivers.body:
When you add people to a group exchange, you choose which side each one is on.

- **Giving time**: the person gives their time. They earn credits, so their balance goes up.
- **Receiving time**: the person receives time. They pay credits, so their balance goes down.

You need at least one person on each side. The page shows how many people are on each side.

In a workshop, the person running it is on **Giving time** and everyone who attends is on **Receiving time**. When a team helps one person, the helpers are on **Giving time** and the person helped is on **Receiving time**.

## Adding yourself

The member search does not show your own name. To take part yourself, use **Add yourself as** on the **Participants** step, and press **Giving time** or **Receiving time**.

For example, if you are leading a workshop, add yourself under **Giving time**. If you are organising help for yourself, add yourself under **Receiving time**.

If you do not add yourself, you organise the exchange but your own balance does not change.

## Before you create it

To take someone off the list, press the cross next to their name.

Everyone under **Receiving time** needs enough time credits in their wallet when the exchange is completed.

split_options.title: The five kinds of group exchange
split_options.summary: What each kind does, who earns and who pays, with an example.
split_options.body:
The kind of group exchange decides how many hours each person earns or pays. You choose it on the **Details** step, under **What kind of group exchange is this?**. **Workshop or class** is already chosen when you open the form.

In every kind, one hour of time is one time credit. People giving time earn credits, and people receiving time pay them.

## Workshop or class

Someone runs a session for a group. The person running it earns the hours they put in. Everyone who attends pays the hours they attended. Any hours left over go to the community's time fund.

Example: Mary runs a 2-hour class for 4 people. Mary earns 2 hours. Each person pays 2 hours. The other 6 hours go to the community time fund.

You answer **How long was the session (in hours)?** once. We fill in that number for everyone you add. Change it for anyone who came for less time. The people giving time cannot earn more than the people attending pay. If they would, the page shows a message and you cannot create the exchange until you fix it.

## A team helping someone

Several people give their time to one person. Each helper earns the hours they spent, and the person helped pays for all of it.

Example: Two volunteers spend 1 hour moving furniture for Tom. Each volunteer earns 1 hour. Tom pays 2 hours.

You answer **How many hours did each helper spend?** once. We fill in that number for every helper. Change it for anyone who spent more or less time. The person helped has no hours to type, because they pay for everything the helpers earn. If more than one person is helped, they share the total equally.

## Share equally

Set one total. Everyone giving time earns an equal share of it, and everyone receiving time pays an equal share.

Example: 6 hours, 2 people giving and 3 receiving: each person giving time earns 3 hours and each person receiving time pays 2.

You enter one number under **Total Hours**.

## Share by amount of effort

Like sharing equally, but you mark who did more. Someone marked 2 gets twice the share of someone marked 1.

Example: Of 6 hours, Ann (marked 2) earns 4 and Ben (marked 1) earns 2.

You enter one number under **Total Hours**, then a share for each person on the **Participants** step. 1 is a normal share. 2 is twice as much. The total is shared by these numbers, separately for the people giving time and the people receiving time.

## Type each person's hours

You enter exactly what each person earns or pays. The total earned must equal the total paid.

Example: Ann earns 3, Ben earns 1, and Cara pays 4.

You type the hours for each person on the **Participants** step. If the total earned and the total paid do not match, the page tells you, and you cannot create the exchange.

## Which one should I choose?

- A class, workshop or session that several people attend: **Workshop or class**.
- Several people helping one person: **A team helping someone**.
- Everyone gave and received about the same: **Share equally**.
- Some people did more than others: **Share by amount of effort**.
- None of these fits: **Type each person's hours**.

Always read **What everyone will earn or pay** before you create the exchange. It shows what each person will earn or pay, and any hours that will go to the community time fund.

confirm_and_complete.title: Starting, confirming and completing a group exchange
confirm_and_complete.summary: The organiser starts it, everyone confirms, then the organiser completes it.
confirm_and_complete.body:
## Starting (organiser)

Open the exchange and press **Start Exchange**. The status becomes **Pending Confirmation**. Every participant gets a notification and an email asking them to confirm.

If the hours do not balance, or a safety rule applies, the exchange does not start and a message explains why.

## Confirming (everyone taking part)

1. Open the exchange from the notification, or from the **Needs Confirmation** tab.
2. Check your role and hours in the participant list.
3. Press **Confirm My Hours**.

The **Confirmed** column shows who has confirmed. If the details change after you confirm, such as the hours or the people taking part, all confirmations are cleared and everyone needs to confirm again.

## Completing (organiser)

When everyone has confirmed, press **Complete Exchange**. Everyone's balance changes at the same time, and each payment appears in the wallet history of the people involved.

> If anyone receiving time does not have enough time credits, the exchange does not complete and no time credits move for anyone. You may need to cancel it and create a new one with different hours.

cancel_group_exchange.title: Cancelling a group exchange
cancel_group_exchange.summary: The organiser can cancel a group exchange before it is completed.
cancel_group_exchange.body:
The organiser can cancel a group exchange at any time before it is completed.

1. Open the exchange.
2. Press **Cancel Exchange**.
3. Press **Cancel Exchange** again to confirm, or **Keep Exchange** to go back.

No hours move. The page shows **Exchange Cancelled**, and the exchange moves to the **Cancelled** tab.

> Cancelling cannot be undone.

A completed group exchange cannot be cancelled. If a completed exchange was wrong, contact your coordinator.

If you are a participant but not the organiser, you cannot cancel. If you no longer want to take part, ask the organiser before they start the exchange.

workshop_community_pot.title: Recording hours for a workshop or group activity
workshop_community_pot.summary: A workshop or class sends any leftover hours to the community time fund by itself.
workshop_community_pot.body:
Group exchanges work well for workshops, classes and other group activities. Choose **Workshop or class** and the page does the sums for you.

## How a workshop works

- The person running the session earns the hours they put in.
- Everyone who attends pays the hours they attended.
- Any hours left over go to your community's time fund.

Mary runs a 2-hour class for 4 people. Mary earns 2 hours. Each person pays 2 hours. The other 6 hours go to the community time fund.

## How to record one

1. Create a group exchange and keep **Workshop or class** chosen.
2. Answer **How long was the session (in hours)?** We fill in that number for everyone you add. Change it for anyone who came for less time.
3. Add the person running the session under **Giving time**. If that is you, use **Add yourself as**.
4. Add everyone who attends under **Receiving time**.
5. Read **What everyone will earn or pay**. It shows what each person earns or pays, and how many hours go to the community time fund. Then create the exchange.

After that it works like any group exchange: you start it, everyone confirms, and you complete it. When it is completed, the leftover hours are added to the community time fund at the same moment everyone's balance changes.

## Nothing else is needed

You do not need a shared member account to hold the leftover hours. Some communities used to set up a "community pot" account for this. With **Workshop or class**, that is no longer needed.

The people running the session cannot earn more than the attendees pay. If they would, the page shows a message. If several people give their time to one person, choose **A team helping someone** instead.

Each person attending needs enough time credits in their wallet when the exchange is completed.

feed.title: Community feed
feed.summary: Share updates and photos, react and comment, and choose what you see.

feed_post_update.title: How do I post an update?
feed_post_update.summary: Write a post for your community feed or for one of your groups.
feed_post_update.body:
You post updates from the [community feed](/feed).

1. Open the [feed](/feed).
2. Press the box that says **What's on your mind?**. A window opens.
3. If the window shows a different form, such as **Listing**, press the **Post** tab at the top.
4. Write your message. You can use up to 5,000 characters. The buttons above the text let you add bold, italics, lists and links.
5. Use the buttons under the text to add an emoji or a GIF. Some browsers also let you speak your post with voice input.
6. If your community uses groups, you see **Post to**. Leave **Public Feed** to share with the whole community, or choose one of your groups.
7. Press **Post**.

A quicker way to reach the **Post** form is the **+** button at the top of the page. Choose **New Post**.

## Other things you can create here

The same window has tabs along the top. Depending on what your community uses, you may see **Listing**, **Event**, **Goal** and **Poll** as well as **Post**. Each tab opens a short form for that kind of item.

> If you close the window part-way through, your browser keeps a draft on this device. It comes back the next time you open the post box.

## Who sees your post

A post to the **Public Feed** is seen by members of your community. A post to a group appears inside that group, for its members.

If you type @ followed by someone's username, they are told you mentioned them.

feed_photos_links.title: Adding photos and links to a post
feed_photos_links.summary: Attach up to 10 photos, describe them for screen readers, and share links with a preview.
feed_photos_links.body:
You can add photos to any post, and links show a preview automatically.

## Adding photos

1. Open the post box on the [feed](/feed).
2. Press the photo area that says **Click or drag photos here**, or drag photos onto it.
3. Choose up to 10 photos. Each one can be up to 10 MB. JPEG, PNG, GIF and WebP files work.
4. Drag the photos to change their order.
5. Press **Add alt text** on each photo and describe what it shows.
6. Write a few words to go with your photos.
7. Press **Post**.

> Alt text is read aloud to people who use screen readers. A short, plain description is best, for example "Volunteers planting trees in the park".

Large photos are made smaller before they upload. This can take a moment.

## Adding a link

Paste a web address into your post. The platform tries to show a preview with the page's title and picture.

Some websites do not allow previews. In that case your post shows the link on its own.

feed_edit_schedule.title: Editing, deleting or scheduling a post
feed_edit_schedule.summary: Change or remove a post you wrote, or choose a time for it to appear.
feed_edit_schedule.body:
You can change or remove your own posts at any time, and you can set a post to appear later.

## Edit or delete a post

1. Find your post on the [feed](/feed).
2. Press the three-dot menu at the top right of the post.
3. Choose **Edit Post**, change the text, and press the button to save it. You can change the words but not the photos.
4. Or choose **Delete Post**, then press **Delete** to confirm. This cannot be undone.

An edited post shows the word **edited** next to the time.

## Schedule a post for later

1. Write your post as usual.
2. Press **Schedule post** under the text.
3. Choose a **Date** and **Time**.
4. Press **Set schedule**.
5. Press **Schedule** to save it.

The post shows **Scheduled for** and the time you chose. It appears on the feed at that time. To go back to posting straight away, press **Clear schedule** before you save.

feed_reactions_comments.title: Reacting and commenting on posts
feed_reactions_comments.summary: Show you like a post, choose a reaction, and join the conversation in the comments.
feed_reactions_comments.body:
You can react to a post with a quick feeling, or write a comment.

## Reactions

Press **Like** under a post. To choose a different reaction, hold your mouse over **Like**, or press and hold it on a phone. You can choose:

- **Like**
- **Love**
- **Laugh**
- **Wow**
- **Sad**
- **Celebrate**
- **Clap**
- **Time Credit**

Press your reaction again to remove it. To see who reacted, press the reaction count.

> The **Time Credit** reaction is a way of saying thank you. It does not send any hours.

## Comments

1. Press **Comment** under the post.
2. Type in the box that says **Write a comment...**.
3. To mention someone, type @ and start typing their name, then choose them from the list.
4. Press the send button.

Under each comment you can press **Reply** to answer it, or **React** to add a reaction.

## Change or remove your comment

Under your own comment, press **Edit** to change it, or **Delete** to remove it. Deleting a comment cannot be undone.

feed_sharing.title: Sharing a post
feed_sharing.summary: Repost, quote, copy a link or send a post to another member.
feed_sharing.body:
Press **Share** under a post to see your sharing options.

- **Repost** shares the post on the feed with your name on it. Press **Remove Repost** to undo it.
- **Quote Post** reposts it with your own comment on top. Type your thoughts and press **Post**.
- **Copy Link** copies the address of the post, so you can paste it anywhere.
- **Share...** opens your device's sharing options. If your device has none, you can choose Email, WhatsApp, X, Facebook or LinkedIn.
- **Send via Message** sends the post to another member in a private message. Search for their name, then press **Send**.

You cannot repost your own post.

> A link to a post only works for people who can sign in to your community. Anyone else sees the sign-in page.

feed_saving.title: Saving posts to read later
feed_saving.summary: Bookmark posts and other items, and sort them into your own collections.
feed_saving.body:
You can save a post so you can find it again later.

Press the bookmark icon on a post. It is saved straight away. Press it again to remove it.

## Collections

Collections are folders for your saved items. On a phone or tablet, press and hold the bookmark icon to choose one:

1. Choose a collection, or **General (no collection)**.
2. To start a new one, press **New collection**, type a name and press **Create collection**.

## Finding saved items

Open [Saved](/saved). Your saved items appear here. You can also save listings, events, jobs, blog articles and group discussions in the same way.

- Use the tabs to show only one kind of item.
- Use **Collection** to show one collection.

On the feed, the **Saved** filter also shows the posts you have saved.

Only you can see what you have saved.

feed_filters.title: Choosing what you see on the feed
feed_filters.summary: Switch between For You and Recent, and show only the kinds of post you want.
feed_filters.body:
You can change the order of the feed and show only the kinds of post you want.

## For You or Recent

At the top of the [feed](/feed), choose:

- **For You**, which puts the posts most likely to interest you first
- **Recent**, which shows the newest posts first

On a **For You** post, press **Why am I seeing this?** to see the reason it was picked.

## Filters

Use the filter buttons to show one kind of item, such as **Posts**, **Events** or **Polls**. **Following** shows posts from your connections. **Saved** shows posts you have saved. Press **All** to see everything again.

Which filters you see depends on the sections your community uses.

## New posts

When new posts arrive while you are reading, a bar appears at the top, such as **1 new post — Tap to see**. Press it to load them.

feed_hide_mute_report.title: Hiding, muting or reporting a post
feed_hide_mute_report.summary: Remove posts you do not want to see, stop seeing one person, or tell the moderators about a problem.
feed_hide_mute_report.body:
Every post has a three-dot menu with options for posts you do not want to see.

1. Press the three-dot menu at the top right of the post.
2. Choose one of these:

- **Hide Post** removes that post from your feed.
- **Not interested** hides it and shows you fewer posts like it.
- **Mute** followed by the person's name stops their posts appearing in your feed. They are not told.
- **Report Post** sends the post to your community's moderators.

> At the moment you cannot undo hiding or muting from your account, so use them with care.

## Reporting a post

1. Choose **Report Post**.
2. In **Reason**, describe what is wrong.
3. Press **Submit Report**.

Your community's moderators then review the report.

If someone is in danger, contact your local emergency services first.

events.title: Events
events.summary: Find community events, say you are going, and run your own.

events_finding.title: How do I find events?
events_finding.summary: Browse upcoming events as a list, a month calendar or an agenda, and narrow them down.
events_finding.body:
All your community's events are on the [Events](/events) page.

## Choose a view

At the top of the page, choose how to see events:

- **List** shows event cards
- **Month** shows a calendar for the whole month
- **Agenda** shows events day by day, starting today

In **Month** and **Agenda**, use **Previous**, **Today** and **Next** to move around. The search and filters below only apply to the **List** view.

## Narrow down the list

- Type in **Search events...** to find an event by name or description.
- Use the time filter to choose **Upcoming**, **Past** or **All Events**.
- Press a category button to see only that kind of event. Press **All** to see every category.
- Press **Near me** and choose a **Radius** to see events close to you. This uses the location saved on your profile.
- Use the venue filter to find events with **Step-free access confirmed**.

Press **Clear filters** to start again.

## What the cards tell you

An event card can show **Full**, a number of places left, or **Cancelled**. It also shows how many people are going or interested. Press a card to open the event.

events_rsvp.title: How do I say I am going to an event?
events_rsvp.summary: Tell the organiser you are coming, join a waiting list when an event is full, or change your mind.
events_rsvp.body:
You reply to an event from its page. This is called an RSVP.

1. Open the event from the [Events](/events) page.
2. Find **RSVP for this event**.
3. Press **Going**, **Interested** or **Not Going**.

**Going** tells the organiser to expect you. It also unlocks the reminders, check-in code and tickets for the event. **Interested** lets you follow the event without promising to come.

## Changing your mind

Press a different button at any time. To remove your reply completely, press your current choice again. If you were going, you are asked to confirm first.

## When an event is full

If there are no places left, the event shows **Full**. You can press **Join Waitlist** to join the waiting list. Your place in the queue is shown, for example **On Waitlist (#3)**. Press **Leave Waitlist** if you no longer want a place.

If your community uses timed offers, you may see **A place is available for you**. Press **Accept place** to take it, or **Decline place** to let someone else have it.

## Other things on the event page

- **Share** copies a link to the event.
- **Attendees** shows who else is coming.
- **Venue accessibility** shows what the organiser knows about access, such as **Step-free access** or a **Hearing loop**. "Not known" means the organiser has not checked.

events_calendar.title: Adding events to your own calendar
events_calendar.summary: Put one event in your phone or computer calendar, or subscribe to all the events you are going to.
events_calendar.body:
You can copy events into the calendar you already use, such as Google Calendar or Outlook.

## Add one event

1. Open the event.
2. Find **Add to your calendar**.
3. Press **Google Calendar** or **Outlook**, or press **Download .ics** for other calendar apps.

## Keep your calendar up to date automatically

Press **Calendar feeds** on the [Events](/events) page. You have two choices:

- **Download community calendar** saves a file with the events you can see. It never includes private locations or meeting links.
- Under **My registered events**, press **Create subscription**. This makes a private web address that your calendar app can follow. It shows the events you are going to.

1. Give the subscription a name if you like.
2. Press **Create subscription**.
3. Press **Copy URL** and paste it into your calendar app's "subscribe" or "add by URL" option.

> The full address is only shown once. Keep it private, because anyone who has it can see the events in it.

If you lose the address or stop using it, press **Revoke** next to the subscription. Your calendar app then stops getting updates. You can create a new one at any time.

Some communities switch calendar feeds off.

events_reminders.title: Setting reminders for an event
events_reminders.summary: Choose when you are reminded about an event you are going to, and how.
events_reminders.body:
Once you have pressed **Going** on an event, you can choose your own reminders.

1. Open the event.
2. Find **Event reminders**. It only appears after you say you are going.
3. Make sure **Enable event reminders** is switched on.
4. Under **Reminder times**, choose **7 days before**, **24 hours before** or **1 hour before**. You can choose more than one.
5. For a different time, type a number in **Custom time in minutes** and press **Add custom time**. For example, 30 means half an hour before.
6. Under **Delivery channels**, choose how to be reminded. The choices include **Email**, **Notification bell** and **Mobile push**.
7. Press **Save reminders**.

You can have up to 10 reminders for one event.

To go back to the normal settings, press **Reset to defaults**.

> Push reminders only reach your phone or browser if you have allowed notifications from the platform on that device.

events_on_the_day.title: Check-in codes, tickets and online events
events_on_the_day.summary: Get your check-in code, reserve a free ticket, and find the link for an online event.
events_on_the_day.body:
Some events ask you to check in when you arrive, have tickets, or take place online. These options appear once you have pressed **Going**.

## Your check-in code

1. Open the event.
2. Find **Your check-in code (optional)**.
3. Press **Create check-in code**.
4. Show the QR code to the event staff when you arrive. You can also press **Copy code** or **Print code**.

> The code is only shown when you create it. Save or print it straight away.

If you lose it, press **Replace code**. The old code stops working. The code does not contain your name or contact details.

Event staff can also find you by name and check you in by hand.

## Tickets

If the organiser has set up tickets, open the **Tickets** tab and press **Reserve ticket**. Your reservations appear under **Your tickets**. To give a ticket back, press **Cancel ticket** and give a reason.

At the moment only free tickets can be reserved.

## Online events

An online event shows **Remote attendance available**. The **Join Meeting** button appears shortly before the start, for people who are going. People on the waiting list cannot see the link.

events_attendance_credits.title: Earning time credits for attending an event
events_attendance_credits.summary: Some events reward you with time credits when you are checked in.
events_attendance_credits.body:
Some events give you time credits for taking part. A time credit is the platform's unit of time: one credit is usually one hour.

Look for the label **Earn** followed by a number of **time credits for attending** on the event page.

## How it works

1. Press **Going** on the event.
2. Go to the event.
3. Get checked in by the event staff, for example with your check-in code.

The credits are added to your [wallet](/wallet) after you are checked in. The wallet entry says **Attendance reward** and the event name.

## Things to know

- Saying you are going is not enough. You must be checked in.
- You can only earn the reward once for each event.
- If you check yourself in to an event you run, you do not get the reward.
- The reward comes from the community. The organiser does not pay it.
- Your community may set a monthly limit on the total credits it gives for attendance. If that limit has been reached, your reward is not paid straight away. An administrator can pay it later.
- An administrator can take a reward back, for example if it was given by mistake. The credits are taken from your wallet, even if this takes your balance below zero. The wallet entry says **Attendance reward reversed** and the event name.
- Most events do not have a reward. Your community's administrators decide which events do, and how much.

This is switched off in most communities. If you do not see the label on any event, your community does not use it.

events_who_can_create.title: Who can create an event?
events_who_can_create.summary: In most communities any member can create events, but some keep this for staff.
events_who_can_create.body:
Your community decides who can create events.

- In most communities, any active member can create an event.
- Some communities only let brokers and administrators create events. A broker is a member of staff who helps members arrange exchanges.
- A few communities only let administrators create events.

## How to tell

If you can create events, you see **Create Event** on the [Events](/events) page and **New Event** under the **+** button at the top of the page.

If your community keeps this for staff, the form shows **Only staff can create Events here**. Ask a community administrator if you would like an event set up.

## Approval

Some communities check new events before anyone else can see them. In that case you press **Submit for review** instead of **Publish event**. Your event shows **Pending review** until an administrator approves it.

events_create.title: How do I create an event?
events_create.summary: Fill in the event form, then publish your event so members can see it.
events_create.body:
You create an event with a short form, then publish it.

1. Open the [Events](/events) page and press **Create Event**.
2. Add a **Cover Image (optional)** if you have one.
3. Type an **Event Title** and a **Description**. The description needs at least 20 characters.
4. Choose a **Category (optional)**.
5. Set the **Start Date** and **Start Time**. Add an end date and time if you know them, or tick **All-day event**.
6. Add a **Location (optional)**. You can then describe the venue's accessibility.
7. Set **Max Attendees (optional)**. Leave it empty for no limit.
8. For an online event, switch on **Allow remote attendance** and paste the **Meeting Link**.
9. Press **Create Event**.

## Publish it

A new event starts as a **Draft event**. Only you can see it. Open it and press **Publish event** when you are ready. If your community checks events first, press **Submit for review**.

## Events for a group

To make an event for a group you belong to, open the group's **Events** tab and press **Create Event** there. The form shows **This event will be associated with your group.**

## Repeating events

Switch on **Make this a recurring event** to create a series. Choose the **Frequency**, such as **Weekly** or **Monthly**, and the days in **Repeat on**. Under **Ends**, choose **After X occurrences**, **On a specific date**, or **Never (rolling schedule)**.

When you edit one date in a series, you are asked to choose **Only this event** or **This and all future events**.

events_manage.title: Managing, cancelling or archiving your event
events_manage.summary: See who is coming, message attendees, check people in, and cancel if plans change.
events_manage.body:
You manage your own events from the event page.

## Edit your event

Open your event and press **Edit**. Change the details and press **Update Event**.

## See who is coming and check people in

Press **Manage**. The management page has sections. You only see the ones you are allowed to use. The main ones are:

- **People**, to see and manage everyone who has replied
- **Check-in**, to scan check-in codes or find people by name on the day
- **Messages to attendees**, to send a message to attendees
- **Team**, to give other members a role, such as a co-organiser or check-in staff

## Cancel an event

1. Open your event and press **Cancel Event**.
2. Type the **Reason for cancellation**.
3. Confirm.

Everyone who replied is told the event is cancelled. For a repeating event, all future dates are cancelled too.

## Archive an event

Press **Archive** to take an event off the member list but keep its history. You can add a reason.

> There is no way to delete an event from the member pages. Cancel or archive it instead.

groups.title: Groups
groups.summary: Join groups of members who share an interest, talk together and share files.

groups_finding.title: How do I find a group?
groups_finding.summary: Browse and search the groups in your community, and see groups picked for you.
groups_finding.body:
You find groups on the [Groups](/groups) page.

- Type in **Search groups...** to find a group by name.
- Press **All Groups**, **My Groups**, **Public** or **Private** to change what is listed. **My Groups** shows the groups you belong to.
- Groups your community wants to highlight appear under **Featured Groups**.
- **Recommended for you** suggests a few groups that match your interests. Each shows a match score, such as **80% match**.

A group you already belong to shows a **Member** label. Press any group to open it.

Press **Load More Groups** at the bottom to see more.

## Groups you cannot see

Private groups only appear in the list if you are already a member. Some groups are hidden completely and you can only join them with an invitation. If someone tells you about a group you cannot find, ask them to send you an invitation.

groups_joining.title: How do I join a group?
groups_joining.summary: Join a public group straight away, or ask to join a private one.
groups_joining.body:
Open the group and press **Join Group**. What happens next depends on the kind of group.

## Public groups

You join straight away. You can now use all its sections.

## Private groups

Pressing **Join Group** sends a request to the group's managers. You see **Join request submitted**. You are told when a manager accepts you.

While you wait, the button shows **Cancel Join Request**. Press it if you change your mind.

## Secret groups

Secret groups do not appear in the list. You can only join one if a manager invites you.

## What you can see before you join

Before you join, you can see the group's name, description and member count. The posts, discussions, files and other sections are only for members. You see **Members Only** or **Join to see the feed** until you join.

> Your community may limit how many groups one member can join. If you reach the limit, you are told when you try to join another.

groups_invitations.title: Group invitations and invite links
groups_invitations.summary: Accept an invitation to a group, or invite people if you manage one.
groups_invitations.body:
A group manager can invite you by email or by sending you a link.

## Accepting an invitation

1. Open the link in the email or message.
2. Sign in if you are asked to.
3. You see **Group Invitation**. Press **Accept Invitation**.
4. You see **Invitation Accepted**. Press **Go to Group**.

An invitation lets you join straight away, even if the group is private or secret.

An email invitation only works for the account with that email address. If you see **This email invitation belongs to a different account.**, sign in with the right account. Invitations can also expire. If yours has, ask the manager for a new one.

## Inviting people (group managers)

1. Open your group and press **Invite**.
2. To share a link, press **Generate Invite Link**, then **Copy**. Anyone with the link can join. A link lasts 14 days.
3. To invite by email, type the addresses in **Or invite by email (comma-separated):**. Add a **Personal message (optional)** if you like.
4. Press **Send Invitations**.

You see a result for each address, such as **Sent** or **Already a member**. Invitations you have sent are listed under **Pending Invitations**. Press **Revoke** to cancel one.

groups_sections.title: What is inside a group?
groups_sections.summary: A quick guide to the tabs you see once you are a member.
groups_sections.body:
Each group has tabs along the top. On a phone they are in a drop-down list. Some tabs sit under **More**.

- **Feed** is for short posts to the group.
- **Discussion** is for longer conversations with a title.
- **Members** lists everyone in the group. **Owner** and **Admin** labels show who runs it.
- **Events** lists the group's events.
- **Files** holds shared documents.
- **Announcements** holds important notices from the managers.
- **Q&A** is for asking questions and voting on answers.
- **Wiki** holds shared pages of information that members write together.
- **Gallery** holds photos and videos.
- **Channels** are chat rooms for the group.
- **Tasks** is a shared to-do list.
- **Challenges** shows group goals set by the managers.
- **Subgroups** appears when a group has smaller groups inside it.

Your community can switch some of these tabs off, so you may not see them all.

Pinned announcements also appear above the tabs with a **Pinned** label.

groups_discussions.title: Posting and discussing in a group
groups_discussions.summary: Share a post with the group, or start a discussion and reply to others.
groups_discussions.body:
There are two ways to talk in a group: the **Feed** tab for short posts, and the **Discussion** tab for longer conversations.

## Post to the group feed

1. Open the group and choose **Feed**.
2. Press **What's on your mind?** and write your post.
3. Press **Create Post**.

You can also choose a group under **Post to** when you write a post on the main community feed.

## Start a discussion

1. Open the group and choose **Discussion**.
2. Press **New Discussion**.
3. Give it a **Title** and write the **Content**.
4. Press **Create Discussion**.

## Reply to a discussion

1. Open the discussion.
2. Type in **Write a reply...**.
3. Send your reply. You see **Reply sent**.

Group posts and discussions are only seen by group members.

groups_files_gallery_wiki.title: Sharing files, photos and wiki pages
groups_files_gallery_wiki.summary: Upload documents and photos to a group and write shared pages together.
groups_files_gallery_wiki.body:
Members can share documents, photos and written pages inside a group.

## Files

1. Open the **Files** tab.
2. Press **Upload File** and choose a file. Each file can be up to 25 MB.
3. Add a **Folder (optional)** or **Description (optional)** if it helps.
4. Upload the file.

Use **Search files...** to find a file. Press a file to download it.

## Gallery

Open the **Gallery** tab to add photos and videos. You can add a **Caption (optional)**. Each item can be up to 50 MB. Use **All**, **Photos** or **Videos** to filter.

## Wiki

The **Wiki** is a set of pages the group writes together, like a shared handbook.

1. Press **New Page**.
2. Type a **Page Title** and the text. Choose a **Parent Page (optional)** to put it under another page.
3. Press **Create Page**.

You can edit pages you wrote or last changed. Press **Edit**, make your change, and add a **Change summary (optional)**. Press **History** to see earlier versions. Group managers can edit any page.

groups_qa_tasks_channels.title: Group Q&A, tasks, channels and challenges
groups_qa_tasks_channels.summary: Ask questions, share out work, chat in channels and follow group goals.
groups_qa_tasks_channels.body:
These tabs help a group work together. Your community may not use all of them.

## Q&A

1. Open **Q&A** and press **Ask Question**.
2. Other members answer with **Post Answer**.
3. Vote answers up or down so the best ones rise to the top.

Sort by **Newest**, **Most Voted** or **Unanswered**. Group managers can mark the best answer.

## Tasks

**Tasks** is a shared to-do list.

1. Press **Add Task**.
2. Give it a **Title**, a **Priority** (**Low**, **Medium**, **High** or **Urgent**), a person under **Assigned to**, and a **Due date**.
3. Move the task through **To Do**, **In Progress** and **Done** as work goes on.

## Channels

**Channels** are chat rooms. Choose a channel, type in **Type a message...** and press **Send**. Group managers create and remove channels.

## Challenges

**Challenges** are goals for the whole group, such as a number of new discussions by a date. The managers set them. You can see the progress, for example **12 / 20 Posts**. Taking part in the group moves the count forward.

groups_notifications_leaving.title: Group notifications and leaving a group
groups_notifications_leaving.summary: Choose how often a group contacts you, or leave it.
groups_notifications_leaving.body:
You can choose how much you hear from each group.

## Notification settings

1. Open the group.
2. Press the megaphone button near the group name. It is labelled **Notification preferences**.
3. Choose a **Notification Frequency**.
4. Switch **Email notifications** and **Push notifications** on or off.
5. Press **Save**.

The frequency choices are:

- **Instant** to hear about new activity as it happens
- **Digest** to get one summary a day
- **Muted** to hear nothing from this group

## Leaving a group

1. Open the group.
2. Press **Leave Group**.
3. Confirm. You see **Left the group**.

You lose access to the group's discussions and files. You can ask to join again later.

> The group's owner cannot leave their own group. If you are the only admin, you also cannot leave. Ask the owner to make another member an admin first.

groups_create.title: How do I start a group?
groups_create.summary: Create a new group, choose who can join, and become its owner.
groups_create.body:
You can start a group from the [Groups](/groups) page.

1. Press **Create Group**.
2. Type a **Group Name** and a **Description** that explains what the group is for.
3. Add a **Location** if the group is for one area.
4. Add a **Group Image** and a **Cover Image** if you like. JPEG, PNG, GIF and WebP work, up to 8 MB.
5. Choose who can join. The choices are explained below.
6. Press **Create Group**.

You become the group's **Owner**.

## Who can join

- **Public** — any member can join straight away
- **Private** — members ask to join and a manager accepts them
- **Secret** — the group is hidden and people join only by invitation. Not every community offers this.

## Things to know

- Some communities check new groups before they appear.
- Some communities do not let members create groups, or limit how many groups one member can own. If you cannot create a group, ask a community administrator.
- Your community may offer **Start from a template (optional)**. A template fills in suggested settings for you.

Only members can see what is posted inside a group, even a public one.

groups_managing.title: Running a group as an owner or admin
groups_managing.summary: What group owners and admins can do, from accepting members to deleting the group.
groups_managing.body:
Each group has an **Owner**, who created it, and can have **Admins** who help run it. Together they are the group's managers.

## What managers can do

- Accept or turn down join requests. Press **View Pending Join Requests**, then **Accept** or **Reject**.
- Invite people with **Invite**.
- Remove a member. Open **Members** and choose **Remove from Group**.
- Post notices with **New Announcement**, and pin them to the top with **Pin this announcement**.
- Change the group's details, pictures, colours and who can join, under **Settings**.
- Set up group **Challenges**, and create or remove **Channels**.
- See the **Analytics** tab, and download member or activity lists.
- Use the **Automation** tab to schedule posts, including repeating posts, and to set a **Welcome Message** for new members.

## What only the owner can do

- Make a member an admin with **Promote to Admin**, or undo it with **Demote to Member**.
- Remove an admin.
- Delete the group. The owner must type the group's name to confirm. This cannot be undone.

> Community administrators can also do all of these things in any group.

blog_resources.title: News, resources and guides
blog_resources.summary: Read community news, find shared documents and look up answers in the knowledge base.

blog_reading.title: Reading community news and blog posts
blog_reading.summary: Find stories, updates and announcements from your community.
blog_reading.body:
Your community shares news and stories on the [Blog & News](/blog) page.

- The newest post is shown large at the top.
- Type in **Search posts...** to find a post.
- Press a category button to see only posts on that subject. Press **All** to see everything.
- Each post shows how long it takes to read, for example **4 min read**.
- Press **Load More Posts** at the bottom to see older posts.

Press a post to read it. Press **Back to Blog** to return to the list.

## Liking and commenting

When you are signed in, you can press **Like** or **Comment** under a post. You can also press **Share** to pass it on.

Blog posts are written by your community's team. Members cannot write blog posts. If you have news to share, you can post it on the community feed instead, or suggest it to your community's administrators.

Blog posts may also appear on the feed. Use the **Blog** filter there to see them.

resources_library.title: Finding and downloading resources
resources_library.summary: Browse documents and files that members and staff have shared.
resources_library.body:
The [Resources](/resources) page holds documents and files shared with the whole community. You might find forms, guides, leaflets or useful lists.

## Find a resource

- Type in **Search resources...** to search by title or description.
- On a computer, choose a category from the **Categories** list on the left. Choose **All Resources** to see everything.
- On a phone, use the filter button to choose a category.

## Download a resource

Press **Download** on the resource. It is saved to your device. The number of downloads is shown next to each file.

You need to be signed in to download.

## Like or comment

Each resource has **Like** and **Comment** buttons, so you can say it helped or ask a question about it.

> Resources are shared by other members as well as staff. Take care with files from people you do not know, as you would with any download.

resources_upload.title: Sharing a resource with your community
resources_upload.summary: Upload a document or picture for all members to use.
resources_upload.body:
Any member can add a file to the [Resources](/resources) page.

1. Open [Resources](/resources).
2. Press **Upload Resource**.
3. Type a **Title**. This is required.
4. Add a **Description** so people know what the file is for.
5. Choose a **Category**.
6. Under **File**, drag your file in or press to choose it.
7. Press **Upload**.

You can upload PDF, Word, Excel, text and CSV files, and JPG, PNG and GIF pictures. Each file can be up to 10 MB.

Your resource appears straight away for everyone in your community. Only share files you have the right to share, and never upload anything with other people's private details.

## Removing your resource

Press the **Delete resource** button on your resource, then press **Delete** to confirm. This cannot be undone.

You cannot change a resource once it is uploaded. To correct it, delete it and upload a new version.

knowledge_base.title: Using the knowledge base
knowledge_base.summary: Look up guides and answers written by your community team.
knowledge_base.body:
The [Knowledge Base](/kb) is a set of guides and answers written by your community's team.

## Find an article

- Type a question or keyword into **Search the knowledge base...**.
- Or press a category tab. **All** shows every article. Articles without a category are under **General**.

Press an article to read it. Some articles include a video, files under **Attachments**, or links under **Related Articles**.

Press **Back to Knowledge Base** to return to the list.

## Tell us if it helped

At the end of each article you see **Was this article helpful?**. Press **Yes** or **No**. This helps the team improve the article. You can change your answer later.

Members cannot write knowledge base articles. If something is missing, contact your community's team.

community_newsletter.title: Getting or stopping the community newsletter
community_newsletter.summary: Choose whether you receive newsletters and community updates by email.
community_newsletter.body:
Your community may send a newsletter by email. You choose whether you get it.

## Start or stop the newsletter

1. Open [Settings](/settings).
2. Choose the **Notifications** tab.
3. Find **Marketing & Communications**.
4. Switch **Marketing Emails** on or off.

When you switch it on, you are asked to confirm. Press **Yes, subscribe me**.

## Unsubscribe from an email

Every newsletter has an unsubscribe link at the bottom. Press it and you see **You're unsubscribed**. You do not need to sign in.

Stopping the newsletter does not stop important account emails, such as messages about your exchanges or your account security.

When you first join, you can also tick **Send me occasional updates and tips** on the sign-up form.

polls_ideas.title: Polls and ideas
polls_ideas.summary: Vote in community polls, ask your own questions and share ideas for challenges.

polls_voting.title: How do I vote in a poll?
