You find podcasts on the **Podcasts** page. Open it from the **Community** menu, or go to [Podcasts](/podcasts).

1. Browse the shows, or type in **Search shows**.
2. Press a show to see its **Episodes**.
3. Press **Listen** on an episode.
4. Press **Play**.

## Using the player

- **Back 15s** and **Forward 30s** skip through the episode.
- The speed buttons play faster, up to 2x.
- If the episode has **Chapters**, press a chapter to jump to it.
- Some episodes have a **Transcript**. Press **Download transcript** to save it as a text file.

On a computer you can use the keyboard. Press Space to play or pause. Use the left and right arrow keys to skip, and the up and down arrow keys to change the volume.

## Listening while you browse

Once an episode is playing, a **Now playing** bar stays on screen as you move around the site. Press **Close player** to stop it.

## Carrying on later

If you stop part way, the episode page offers **Resume from** a time, or **Start over**. This is remembered on the device you used. It does not carry over to another phone or computer.

following_and_reporting_podcasts.title: Following shows and reporting episodes
following_and_reporting_podcasts.summary: Get told about new episodes, react to episodes and report a problem.
following_and_reporting_podcasts.body:
You can follow a show to hear about new episodes.

## Following a show

1. Open the show's page.
2. Press **Follow show**.
3. You see **Show followed.**

When a new episode is published, you get a notification. To stop, press **Unfollow show**.

Some public shows also have an **RSS feed** button. You can add this address to a podcast app on your phone.

## Reacting to an episode

If your community allows it, an episode page has a **React** button. Press it to show you liked the episode. Press it again to remove your reaction.

## Reporting an episode

If an episode is harmful, misleading or breaks someone's rights, please report it.

1. Open the episode page.
2. Press **Report**.
3. Choose a **Reason**: **Safety or harm**, **Spam or misleading content**, **Copyright or rights concern** or **Other**.
4. Add **Details for moderators** to explain the problem.
5. Press **Send report**.

You see **Report sent to moderators.** The community's moderators then review the episode.

creating_a_podcast.title: How do I start my own podcast show?
creating_a_podcast.summary: Create a show and add episodes in the Podcast Studio.
creating_a_podcast.body:
You make shows and episodes in the **Podcast Studio**. Go to [Podcast Studio](/podcasts/studio), or press **Create show** on the Podcasts page.

In most communities any member can create a show. If you are not allowed, the studio tells you.

## Creating a show

1. Under **Create show**, enter a **Show title**.
2. Choose a **Category** and add **Show artwork** if you have it.
3. Choose the **Visibility**. **Public** means anyone can listen. Some communities also offer **Members** and **Private**.
4. Add a **Summary** and **Description**.
5. Press **Create show**.

## Adding an episode

1. Under **Add episode**, choose the **Show**.
2. Enter an **Episode title**.
3. Upload your recording under **Hosted audio file**, or paste a web address in **Audio URL**.
4. Add a **Summary**, and a **Transcript** if you can. A transcript helps people who cannot hear the audio.
5. To release it later, use **Schedule publication**.
6. Press **Add episode**.

> Only upload audio you have the right to share, and get permission from anyone you record.

## Managing your shows

Your shows appear under **My shows**. Here you can edit, publish, archive or delete shows and episodes. In some communities a moderator checks new shows and episodes first. These show **Pending review** until approved.

**Listener stats** shows how many people listened to your episodes.

caring_community.title: Caring Community
caring_community.summary: Ask for everyday care, record kindness, support people you care for and raise a concern.

what_is_caring_community.title: What is the Caring Community?
what_is_caring_community.summary: A place in your community for everyday care, such as lifts, shopping and company.
what_is_caring_community.body:
The Caring Community is a part of the platform for everyday care between neighbours. Examples are a lift to an appointment, help with shopping, or some company for an afternoon.

Open the **Community** menu and choose **Caring Community**, or go to [Caring Community](/caring-community).

It works alongside timebanking. Time you give is counted in the same time credits as the rest of the platform. There is one balance, not a separate currency.

## What you can do from the hub

The hub groups its options:

- **Get help**: ask for practical support and see your support relationships.
- **Give help**: record a kindness, offer your time or log volunteering hours.
- **Your hours**: for example, gift some of your hours to someone else.
- **Safety & updates**: raise a safeguarding concern.

You only see options that your community has switched on.

## It is new

The hub says the Caring Community is brand new, and that some parts are early previews. It depends on neighbours volunteering their time. If your community also uses volunteering, press **I'd like to help** to see volunteering opportunities.

> The first time you visit, you may be asked **What brings you here today?** Your answer only changes which button is shown first. You can change it at any time.

requesting_care_help.title: How do I ask for help?
requesting_care_help.summary: Tell your community what practical help you need and how to contact you.
requesting_care_help.body:
You ask for help with the **Request Help** form.

1. On the [Caring Community](/caring-community) hub, press **I need some help** or **Request help**. You can also go straight to [Request Help](/caring-community/request-help).
2. Under **What kind of help do you need?**, describe what you need in your own words. You can use up to 500 characters.
3. Under **When do you need it?**, say when. For example, Tuesday afternoons, or as soon as possible.
4. Under **How should we contact you?**, choose **By phone**, **By message** or **Either is fine**.
5. Press **Request Help**.

You see **Request Received**.

## Speaking instead of typing

On some devices you can press **Tap to speak your request** and say what you need. The form is filled in from your recording. Check it carefully before you press **Request Help**. Nothing is sent until you press it.

## What happens next

Your request is saved for your community's care coordinators to review. You cannot see or change your request afterwards on this page.

> If you need help soon, or have not heard back, contact your community coordinator directly. If someone is in danger or needs urgent medical help, contact your local emergency services.

offering_a_favour.title: How do I record a favour?
offering_a_favour.summary: Record an act of kindness you did for someone. No time credits are involved.
offering_a_favour.body:
A favour is a small act of kindness you want to record. Examples are carrying shopping, giving a lift or sharing a meal. Favours do not earn or cost time credits.

1. On the [Caring Community](/caring-community) hub, press **Offer a Favour**. You can also go to [Offer a Favour](/caring-community/offer-favour).
2. Under **What did you do to help?**, describe what you did.
3. Choose a **Category** if you like, such as **Companionship** or **Transport**.
4. Under **When?**, choose the date. It starts as today.
5. Press **Record Favour**.

You see **Thank You!** Your community's coordinators can see the favours members record.

## Favours or time credits?

- Record a favour for an informal kindness you do not want credits for.
- To earn time credits for help you give, use timebanking or volunteering instead. On the hub, press **Offer time** or **Log hours**.

support_relationships.title: What are support relationships?
support_relationships.summary: See the regular support you give or receive, and pause or end it.
support_relationships.body:
A support relationship is a regular arrangement between a **Supporter**, who gives help, and a **Recipient**, who receives it. Your community's coordinators set these up. You cannot start one yourself.

To see yours, press **My Support Relationships** on the [Caring Community](/caring-community) hub, or go to [My Support Relationships](/caring-community/my-relationships).

## What each one shows

- The other person's name, and whether you are the **Supporter** or **Recipient**.
- How often you meet, such as **Weekly**, and the hours expected.
- The **Next check-in** date, or **Overdue** if it has passed.
- **Recent hours logged**, with whether each entry is **Approved**, **Pending** or **Declined**. Coordinators record these hours.

## Pausing, resuming or ending

- Press **Pause** to stop for a while. The status changes to **Paused**. Press **Resume** when you are ready to start again.
- Press **End relationship** to stop for good. This cannot be undone. Ended relationships no longer appear on this page.

> The other person is not told automatically when you pause or end a relationship. Please let them know yourself, or ask your coordinator to.

report_a_concern.title: How do I report a safeguarding concern?
report_a_concern.summary: Tell your community's safeguarding staff if you are worried someone is at risk of harm.
report_a_concern.body:
If you are worried that someone is being harmed, neglected or taken advantage of, you can report it.

> If someone is in immediate danger, contact your local emergency services first. Then make a report here.

1. On the [Caring Community](/caring-community) hub, press **Report a Concern**. You can also go to [Report a Safeguarding Concern](/caring-community/safeguarding/report).
2. Under **What kind of concern is this?**, choose the closest match.
3. Under **How urgent is this?**, choose from **Critical (immediate risk to a person)** to **Low (worth flagging)**.
4. Under **Describe your concern**, say what you saw or heard, when, and who was involved.
5. If you have a link to evidence, add it under **Evidence link (optional)**.
6. Press **Submit Report**.

You see **Report Submitted**.

## The optional boxes for people and organisations

**Person involved (optional)** and **Organisation involved (optional)** ask for a member or organisation number. If you do not know it, leave these empty. Give names in your description instead.

## Who sees your report

Your report is seen by the people who handle safeguarding in your community, such as coordinators and administrators. They can see that you made the report. The person you report about cannot see your report.

Choose **Critical** only when a person is at immediate risk. In an emergency, always contact your local emergency services as well.

my_safeguarding_reports.title: Checking on a concern you reported
my_safeguarding_reports.summary: See the status of the safeguarding reports you have made.
my_safeguarding_reports.body:
You can see the safeguarding reports you have made on the **My Safeguarding Reports** page.

Go to [My Safeguarding Reports](/caring-community/safeguarding/my-reports). You can also press **View my reports** straight after you submit a report.

Each report shows how urgent it is, the type of concern, the start of your description and the date you sent it.

## What the statuses mean

- **Submitted**: your report has been received.
- **Triaged**: staff have looked at it and decided how to handle it.
- **Under investigation**: staff are looking into it.
- **Resolved**: staff have finished dealing with it.
- **Dismissed**: staff decided no further action was needed.

You may also see **Escalated**. This means the report has been raised for more urgent attention.

> You are not sent a notification when the status changes. Come back to this page to check. This page does not show what action was taken. If you are still worried, contact your community coordinator directly.

linking_a_care_receiver.title: How do I link to someone I care for?
linking_a_care_receiver.summary: Ask to be recorded as the caregiver of a member you already look after.
linking_a_care_receiver.body:
If you already look after a member informally, you can ask to be linked as their caregiver. This gives you some caregiver tools, such as asking for help on their behalf.

1. On the [Caring Community](/caring-community) hub, press **Become a caregiver**. You can also go to [Link a Care Receiver](/caring-community/caregiver/link).
2. Under **Find member**, type at least 2 letters of their name and choose them.
3. Choose the **Relationship**: **Family member**, **Friend**, **Neighbour** or **Professional carer**.
4. Enter the date under **Care started**.
5. Add **Notes** if you like. The person you care for can see these.
6. Press **Link a care receiver**.

## The checks before the link is active

A link does not start straight away. It goes through two checks:

1. The person you care for is told and must agree. The status shows **Waiting for the care recipient**.
2. Your community's staff then review it for safeguarding. The status shows **Waiting for staff safeguarding review**.

When both are done, the status shows **Active** and you are both told. If the link is refused, it shows **Not approved**.

> If a request is declined or withdrawn, you must wait 7 days before asking again.

caregiver_dashboard.title: Using the Caregiver Dashboard
caregiver_dashboard.summary: See the people you care for, their care schedule, and answer caregiver requests about you.
caregiver_dashboard.body:
The **Caregiver Dashboard** brings together the people you care for. Go to [Caregiver Dashboard](/caring-community/caregiver).

## If you are a caregiver

**People I care for** lists the people you are linked to. For each active link you can:

- Press **View care schedule** to see **Upcoming care** and **Recent care**.
- Press **Request help on their behalf** to open the Request Help form for them.

To add someone, press **Link a care receiver**.

If you log a lot of volunteering hours in one week, the dashboard shows a reminder to rest. Looking after yourself matters too.

## If someone asks to be your caregiver

You get a notification when a member asks to be linked as your caregiver. The link in the notification opens this dashboard. Under **Caregiver requests about me**:

- Press **Confirm relationship** only if you know this person and agree.
- Press **Reject request** if you do not agree.

No caregiver tools are given to the other person until you agree and staff have checked the request.

> If you did not expect a request, or feel pressured, press **Reject request**. Then talk to your community coordinator.

gifting_hours.title: How do I gift hours to someone?
gifting_hours.summary: Give some of your time credits to family, friends or anyone who needs them.
gifting_hours.body:
You can give some of your banked hours to another member of your community. These are the same time credits as in your wallet.

1. On the [Caring Community](/caring-community) hub, press **Gift Hours**. You can also go to [Gift Your Hours](/caring-community/hour-gift).
2. On the **Send** tab, find the person under **Who would you like to gift hours to?**. Type at least 2 letters of their name.
3. Enter **How many hours?**. You can see how many hours you have available.
4. Add a personal message if you like.
5. Press **Gift Hours**.
6. Check the details and press **Yes, gift hours**.

The hours leave your wallet straight away. They reach the other person when they accept.

> The other person may not get a notification about your gift. Let them know you have sent it, and ask them to open **Gift Hours** and check their **Inbox**.

## Receiving a gift

Open the **Inbox** tab. Press **Accept** to add the hours to your wallet. Press **Decline** to send them back.

## Changing your mind

On the **Sent** tab, a gift waiting to be accepted shows **Awaiting acceptance**. Press **Withdraw gift** to cancel it. The hours come back to you.

caring_markt.title: Browsing offers and local goods in one place
caring_markt.summary: The Marktplatz page shows time-credit offers and local goods together, so you can browse both at once.
caring_markt.body:
The **Marktplatz** page brings together two kinds of things your community shares: help offered for time credits, and goods and services for sale.

Open the [Caring Community](/caring-community) page and press **Marktplatz**, or go straight to [Marktplatz](/caring-community/markt).

## Choosing what to see

Use the tabs at the top:

- **All** shows both kinds together.
- **Time Credits** shows offers and requests members have listed for time credits.
- **Goods & Services** shows items from the marketplace, if your community uses it.

Each card has a label, **Time Credits** or **Goods & Services**, so you can tell them apart.

## Looking nearer to home

- If your community is split into areas, choose one under **Area**.
- Press **Near me** to see things close to you. This needs a location on your profile. If you have not set one, you are asked to add it.

## Opening an item

Press **View** on a card. This opens the full listing or item, where you can respond, message the person or buy.

The page shows only the newest items. To see everything, use the listings or marketplace pages themselves.

caring_hour_transfer.title: Moving your hours to another community
caring_hour_transfer.summary: If you move, you can ask to transfer time credits to a partner community. A coordinator reviews every request.
caring_hour_transfer.body:
If you are moving to another community, you can ask for some of your time credits to go with you. Nothing moves until a coordinator approves it.

## Before you start

- The new community must be a partner of your community.
- You usually need an account there, using the same email address you use here.
- You can transfer up to 24 hours in one request.
- You need at least that many hours in your wallet.

## Asking for a transfer

1. Open the [Caring Community](/caring-community) page and press the hour transfer option, or go to [Transfer Your Banked Hours](/caring-community/hour-transfer).
2. Press **Browse communities** and choose the new community, then press **Select**.
3. If no communities are listed, type the community's short name under **Or enter a community slug manually**. Ask the new community for it.
4. Enter the **Hours to transfer**.
5. Add a **Reason (optional)**.
6. Press **Request Transfer**.

You see **Transfer request submitted. A coordinator will review it before hours move.**

## What happens next

Your request appears under **Your transfer history** as **Awaiting approval**. The hours stay in your wallet until a coordinator approves. The status then changes, for example to **Sent** or **Completed**, or to **Rejected**.

You cannot cancel a request yourself. Contact a coordinator if you change your mind.

> If you see **Could not request the transfer. Please try again.**, check the community name and your balance. The new community may not be a partner, or may not have an account with your email. A coordinator can help.

caring_trust_tier.title: What is my trust tier?
caring_trust_tier.summary: Your trust tier reflects your volunteering, reviews and identity check. See what you need for the next tier.
caring_trust_tier.body:
Your trust tier is a simple sign of how established you are in the Caring Community. It is worked out from three things.

Open [My Trust Level](/caring-community/my-trust-tier) to see yours.

## The three signals

- **Volunteer hours logged**: volunteering hours that have been approved.
- **Positive reviews received**: reviews other members have left for you.
- **Identity verified**: whether you have completed an identity check, if your community offers one.

Each signal shows your progress, such as **3 of 10**, and whether it is **Achieved** or **In progress**.

## The tiers

The tiers, from first to last, are **Newcomer**, **Member**, **Trusted**, **Verified** and **Coordinator**. Your community decides what each one needs. The page shows **Your current tier**, the **Next tier** and your **Progress to** the next one.

## What the tier does not do

Your tier does not give you extra permissions. Reaching the **Coordinator** tier does not make you one of your community's coordinators.

Your tier is worked out again each time you open the page, so it changes as your hours and reviews grow.

caring_data_export.title: Downloading your Caring Community data
caring_data_export.summary: Download a file of the information you have added to the Caring Community, such as hours, gifts and reports.
caring_data_export.body:
You can download a copy of the information you have added to the Caring Community.

1. Go to [My data export](/caring-community/my-data-export).
2. Press **Download my data (JSON)**.
3. Wait while it says **Preparing your export…**.

You see **Your export has started downloading.** The file is saved to your device.

## What is in the file

It covers your Caring Community activity only, for example:

- the hours you have logged
- your support relationships
- help requests and favours
- hours you have gifted or transferred
- safeguarding reports you have made

It does not include other members' personal information.

The file is in JSON format. This is a plain text format that computers read easily. It may look untidy if you open it yourself. If you need another format, contact your community coordinator.

## Your whole account

This file does not cover the rest of your account, such as your messages or listings. For a copy of your whole account, use [Download your data](/settings/data-export) in your settings.

premium_offers.title: Donations and partner venues
premium_offers.summary: Support your community with a donation, and use your membership pass at local venues.

donating_to_your_community.title: How do I donate to my community?
donating_to_your_community.summary: Give a one-off gift or set up a regular donation by card.
donating_to_your_community.body:
If your community accepts donations, you can give money by card to support it. Open the **Community** menu and choose **Donate**, or go to [Donate](/premium).

## Giving once

1. Press **Make a one-off donation**.
2. Enter the **Amount** and choose a **Fund** if you want your money used for something in particular. Donations are taken in your community's currency, shown next to the amount.
3. Add a message, or choose **Donate anonymously**, if you like.
4. Press **Continue to Payment**, then enter your card details and pay.

When it works, you see **Thank You!** and can view your receipt.

## Giving regularly

Your community may offer support levels for regular giving.

1. Choose **Monthly** or **Yearly** at the top of the page.
2. Pick a support level and press **Donate regularly**.
3. You are taken to a secure payment page run by Stripe, a payment company. Enter your card details there.
4. When you return, you see **You are all set!**

If you see **Still processing…**, your payment is going through. Press **Check status** after a moment.

> Donations are gifts to your community. Giving regularly does not unlock extra features on the platform, and it does not change how other members see you or match with you.

Money donations are separate from time credits. You earn time credits by giving your time.

managing_regular_donation.title: Changing or cancelling a regular donation
managing_regular_donation.summary: See your regular donation, update your card or stop giving.
managing_regular_donation.body:
You manage a regular donation on the **My Support** page. Go to [My Support](/premium/manage).

The page shows your support level, whether you pay **Billed monthly** or **Billed yearly**, and the **Next billing** date.

## Updating your card or payment details

Press **Manage in Stripe**. This opens Stripe's billing page, where you can update your card.

## Cancelling

1. Press **Cancel regular donation**.
2. Confirm that you want to cancel.

You see **Regular donation will end at the period end**. You are not charged again. Your donation stays active until the end of the period you have already paid for.

## If a payment fails

The page shows a message asking you to update your card by a date. Press **Manage in Stripe** to update it.

## Changing your support level

Before choosing a new level, cancel your current regular donation. This makes sure you are not paying for two at once. Then press **Change support level** and choose the new level.

If you see **No active regular donation**, you are not giving regularly at the moment. Press **View support levels** to start.

partner_venue_pass.title: Using your membership pass at partner venues
partner_venue_pass.summary: Find local venues that welcome members and show your pass when you visit.
partner_venue_pass.body:
Partner venues are local places, such as cafés, shops and community spaces, that welcome members of your community.

## Finding venues

Open the **Community** menu and choose **Partner venues**, or go to [Partner venues](/venues). Each venue shows what it offers members, its address and a link to its website.

## Your membership pass

1. Press **My pass** on the venues page, or go to [My membership pass](/venues/pass). You can also press **My venue pass** in your wallet.
2. A QR code appears on screen.
3. When you visit a partner venue, show this code to the staff.
4. The staff scan it and confirm your visit.

Your visits are listed under **Recent visits**. A visit can be recorded once per venue per day.

> The platform only records your visit. It does not take any payment or apply any discount. Any offer is given by the venue itself.

## Keeping your pass safe

If you think someone has copied your code, press **Replace my code**. Your old code then stops working.

## If you are venue staff

If your community has added you as staff at a venue, scan a member's pass with your phone camera. Sign in if asked, then press **Record visit**.

broker_role.title: Your role as a broker
broker_role.summary: What brokers and coordinators do, what they can and cannot change, and how to find your way around the Broker Panel.

broker_what_is_a_broker.title: What is a broker or coordinator?
broker_what_is_a_broker.summary: Brokers and coordinators run the timebank day to day, using a separate part of the site called the Broker Panel.
broker_what_is_a_broker.body:
A broker is the person who runs your timebank day to day. Some communities say "coordinator" instead. Both roles open the same **Broker Panel**.

A broker helps members swap time fairly and safely. Typical tasks are:

- welcoming new members and approving them when your community checks people before they join
- signing off exchanges that need a broker's approval
- reading messages that have been copied to brokers for safeguarding
- recording your community's vetting decisions
- removing posts, comments and reviews that break the rules
- helping members who find the website hard to use

You do this work in the **Broker Panel**. It is a separate part of the site, built for day-to-day tasks. You still have your own member account as well. You can post listings and swap time like any other member.

## A broker is not a junior admin

A broker and a community admin have different jobs. An admin sets up the community: its settings, its sections and its rules. A broker works inside those rules with members. For that reason brokers are not allowed into the admin panel, and some settings in the Broker Panel are marked **Admin only**.

> The decisions you make in the Broker Panel, such as approvals, reviews and balance changes, are recorded with your name. This keeps a clear record for your community.

broker_can_and_cannot.title: What can a broker do, and what is only for admins?
broker_can_and_cannot.summary: A plain list of the tasks brokers can do, and the ones that need a community admin.
broker_can_and_cannot.body:
Brokers look after members and daily activity. Admins look after the community's setup.

## You can

- approve, suspend and reactivate ordinary members
- edit a member's name, phone, location, tagline and bio
- resend a verification email, send a password reset, or reset two-factor sign-in
- adjust an ordinary member's time balance, with a reason
- keep private notes about members
- approve or reject exchanges that need broker approval
- tag listings with a risk level
- review message copies, place members under monitoring and turn off their messaging
- confirm, renew or revoke vetting decisions
- record insurance certificates
- remove posts, comments and reviews that break the rules, and close reports
- change the safeguarding options members can choose
- change the Broker Panel settings that are not marked **Admin only**

## Only an admin can

- change community settings, sections and branding
- give someone a role, such as broker or admin
- create, import, ban or delete accounts
- reactivate a member who was banned (you can lift an ordinary suspension)
- choose the community's safeguarding jurisdiction
- pay hours out of the Community Fund
- set rewards for attending events

## Checks that protect you

To keep things fair, the site stops you acting where you have a personal interest. You cannot:

- approve or reject an exchange you are part of
- moderate content you wrote or are part of
- close a report you made
- close a report about you, or about something that is yours, such as your post, listing or comment, or a review you wrote or received
- adjust your own balance, or another broker's or an admin's

You also cannot change another broker's or an admin's account. If you try, you will see an error. Ask another broker or an admin to help instead.

broker_becoming_a_broker.title: How does someone become a broker?
broker_becoming_a_broker.summary: A community admin gives the broker role from the admin panel. You then see the Broker Panel link.
broker_becoming_a_broker.body:
Only a community admin can make someone a broker. You cannot ask for the role from your own account.

The admin opens the member's account in the admin panel. They set **Role** to **Broker** and save.

## After you become a broker

1. Sign in as usual.
2. Look at the bar at the top of the page. You now see **Broker Panel**.
3. Press **Broker Panel** to open it.

If you do not see the link, sign out and sign in again. If it is still missing, ask your admin to check your role.

## When the role ends

If you stop being a broker, ask your admin to change your role back to **Member**. The Broker Panel link then disappears. Your notes and decisions stay on record with your name.

> Brokers who are also admins see the admin panel link instead. From inside the Broker Panel, admins also see **Full Admin Panel** at the bottom of the menu.

broker_finding_your_way.title: Finding your way around the Broker Panel
broker_finding_your_way.summary: The menu, the top bar, the search box and the red counters explained.
broker_finding_your_way.body:
The Broker Panel has a menu on the left and a bar along the top. On a phone, press the menu button to open the menu.

## The menu

The menu is grouped by type of work:

- **Overview**: **Dashboard**, which shows what needs your attention now
- **Daily Workflow**: **Members**, **Onboarding**, **Exchanges**, **Match Approvals** and **Messages**
- **Moderation**: **Content Queue**, **Feed Posts**, **Comments**, **Reviews** and **Reports**
- **Compliance & Oversight**: **Safeguarding**, **Safeguarding Options**, **Vetting confirmations**, **User Monitoring**, **Risk Tags** and **Insurance**
- **Records**: **Review Archive**
- **Settings**: **Configuration** and **Help**

Some items only appear if your community uses that section. For example, **Exchanges** and **Match Approvals** only appear when your community uses the exchange workflow.

A red number next to a menu item shows how many things are waiting. The numbers update about once a minute.

## The top bar

- **Back to Site** takes you back to the member side of the site.
- **Search** opens a box where you type a page name, such as "vetting", and jump straight to it. You can also press Ctrl and K together (Cmd and K on a Mac).
- **Help Center** opens the Broker Panel's own guidance page.
- The bell opens your notifications.
- Your name opens a menu with **My Profile** and **Sign Out**.

To make the menu narrower, press **Collapse sidebar** at the top of the menu.

broker_dashboard.title: Using the Broker Dashboard
broker_dashboard.summary: The dashboard shows what is waiting for you, key counts and some recent broker actions.
broker_dashboard.body:
The **Broker Dashboard** is the first page you see. It tells you what needs you now.

## What needs you now

At the top, a box lists the kinds of work waiting for review, with the most urgent first. Press any line to go straight to that list. When nothing is waiting you see **All clear**.

## The counters

Below that are counters. Each one opens the matching list, already filtered:

- **Pending Exchanges**: exchanges waiting for broker approval
- **Unreviewed Messages**: message copies nobody has reviewed yet
- **High Risk Listings**: listings tagged high risk
- **Monitored Users**: members under monitoring
- **Vetting review requests**: members who asked for a vetting review
- **Safeguarding Alerts**: urgent safeguarding items
- **Support needs not yet seen**: members who told us they would like extra support and whom no broker has marked as seen yet

If a counter shows a dash, it could not load. Press **Refresh** to try again.

## Quick Access and Recent Activity

**Quick Access** has shortcuts to the main tools.

**Recent Activity** lists the latest broker actions of some kinds only: exchange approvals and rejections, message reviews, risk tags, monitoring changes, Broker Panel setting changes and insurance records. It shows who did what and when.

It does not show member approvals or suspensions, balance changes, notes, content moderation, reports or vetting decisions. To check whether someone else has already dealt with one of these, look at the item itself, such as the member's record or notes.

broker_configuration.title: Changing the Broker Panel settings
broker_configuration.summary: Which messages are copied to brokers and how exchange approval works are set in Configuration.
broker_configuration.body:
[Configuration](/broker/configuration) holds the settings for broker work in your community. Settings marked **Admin only** can only be changed by an admin. You can see them, but not change them.

After changing anything, press **Save Changes**. **Unsaved changes** shows until you do.

## Settings brokers can change

These decide which messages are copied to brokers:

- **Copy first contact between members**: copies the first message between any two members.
- **Copy messages from new members**: copies messages from members who joined recently. **New-member monitoring window (days)** sets how long "recently" is.
- **Copy messages on high-risk listings**: copies messages about listings tagged high or critical risk.
- **Random sample percentage**: copies this share of all other messages at random, for spot checks. For example, 5 means about 5 in every 100. At 100, every message is copied, the same as **Copy all messages to broker**, so agree any high number with your admin first.
- **Archive retention (days)**: how long reviewed, unflagged message copies are kept before they are deleted.

## Settings only an admin can change

- **Broker messaging enabled**: the main switch. When it is off, no messages are copied to brokers, whatever the other settings say.
- **Copy all messages to broker**: copies every message between members.
- **Broker approval required**: exchanges wait for a broker's approval.
- **Auto-approve low-risk exchanges**: lets most exchanges go ahead without a broker.
- **Max hours without approval**: with auto-approve on, exchanges above this many hours still need a broker.
- **Insurance tracking enabled**: lets members add insurance records in their settings.

## Choosing settings

Copying more messages gives brokers more to read. It also reaches further into members' privacy. Agree the settings with your admin and safeguarding lead. Choose the lightest settings that keep people safe.

> This guide describes the settings that change how the site behaves. If you are unsure what a setting does, ask your admin before changing it.

broker_members.title: Looking after members
broker_members.summary: Approve new members, keep notes, help people with their accounts and correct balances.

broker_approve_new_members.title: How do I approve a new member?
broker_approve_new_members.summary: New registrations wait in the Pending tab until a broker or admin approves them.
broker_approve_new_members.body:
If your community checks people before they can take part, each new registration waits for approval. You approve them from **Members** or **Onboarding**.

1. Open [Members](/broker/members).
2. Press the **Pending** tab. The red number on **Members** in the menu shows how many are waiting.
3. Find the person. Press the three-dot menu at the end of their row and choose **View details** to check their details first.
4. Press the three-dot menu again and choose **Approve**.
5. Press **Approve** again to confirm.

The member can now sign in and use the site. They get a welcome email and a notification.

## Starting hours

When you approve someone, the site adds starting hours to their balance. This is 5 hours unless an admin has set a different starting balance. If your admin has set it to 0, no hours are added. Each member only ever gets their starting hours once.

## Approving several people at once

1. On the **Pending** tab, tick the box next to each person.
2. Press **Approve selected**.

Starting hours are added for each person you approve this way too. Use this only when you have already checked each person.

## If you do not want to approve someone

There is no reject button in the Broker Panel. Leave the person pending and talk to your admin or your community's lead about what to do. Do not approve someone to "sort it out later".

> The [Onboarding](/broker/onboarding) page has the same pending list under **Pending Approvals**, with an **Approve** option in each row's menu.

broker_members_list.title: Finding and filtering members
broker_members_list.summary: Search the member list and use tabs to find people who are pending, suspended or have never signed in.
broker_members_list.body:
[Members](/broker/members) lists everyone in your community. Across the top you see **Total members**, **Pending approval**, **Active members** and **Suspended members**. Press a counter to open that list.

## Tabs

- **All**: everyone
- **Pending**: waiting for approval
- **Active**: approved members who can use the site
- **Suspended**: members who cannot sign in at the moment
- **Never logged in**: approved members who have not signed in yet
- **Onboarding incomplete**: members who have not finished the setup steps

The last two tabs are a good place to start when you want to offer help to people who are stuck.

## Searching and filtering

- Type a name or email into **Search members...**.
- Use **Filter by role** to show only members, brokers or admins, for example.

## What each row shows

Each row shows the member's name, status, role, whether their email is verified, their balance in hours, when they were last active and when they joined.

## Row actions

Press the three-dot menu at the end of a row to:

- **View details**: open the member's full record
- **View Profile**: see their public profile in a new tab
- **Send Message**: start a message to them in a new tab
- **Notes**: read or add private notes
- **Check Vetting**: open their vetting record
- **Approve**, **Suspend** or **Reactivate**, depending on their status

broker_member_details.title: Viewing a member's full record
broker_member_details.summary: The member record brings together their status, balance, compliance records, notes and account actions.
broker_member_details.body:
Open a member's record to see everything about them in one place.

1. Open [Members](/broker/members).
2. Press the three-dot menu on their row.
3. Choose **View details**.

At the top you see their name, status, role, email address and whether the email is verified.

## Tabs in the record

- **Overview**: their balance, when they joined, when they were last active, and whether they finished onboarding. A **Membership journey** line shows when they registered, verified their email and were approved.
- **Compliance**: their **Contact attestation** (vetting decision), any **Insurance certificates** and any **Consents** they have given.
- **Notes**: private notes from brokers and admins.
- **Actions**: account tools, such as approving, suspending, sending a password reset or adjusting their balance. You can also edit parts of their profile here.

## Editing a profile

On the **Actions** tab, press **Edit** next to **Profile**. You can change **First name**, **Last name**, **Phone**, **Location**, **Tagline** and **Bio**. Press **Save changes**.

You cannot change a member's email address, role or status here. Ask an admin if one of these needs to change.

> Only change a member's profile when they ask you to, or when it breaks your community's rules. Tell them what you changed.

broker_member_notes.title: Keeping private notes about a member
broker_member_notes.summary: Notes help brokers share context. Members cannot see them.
broker_member_notes.body:
Notes let brokers and admins keep a shared record about a member. Members never see these notes.

## Adding a note

1. Open [Members](/broker/members).
2. Press the notes button on the member's row, or choose **Notes** from the three-dot menu. You can also use the **Notes** tab in the member's record.
3. Choose a **Category**: **General**, **Outreach**, **Support**, **Onboarding**, **Concern** or **Follow up**.
4. Type your note in the box.
5. Press the send button.

Each note shows who wrote it and when.

## Managing notes

- **Pin note** keeps an important note at the top. Only an admin can pin a note.
- **Edit note** corrects a note. Only an admin can edit a note.
- **Delete note** removes a note. Only an admin can delete one. If you wrote something wrong, add a new note that corrects it.

## What to write

Write facts, not opinions. Good notes are short and useful to the next broker, for example: "Called 3 May. Prefers phone to email. Wants help finding gardening work."

> Do not record vetting certificates, health details or other sensitive information in notes unless your community's rules say you may. A member can ask to see the information you hold about them.

broker_suspend_member.title: Suspending or reactivating a member
broker_suspend_member.summary: Suspending stops a member signing in. You can reactivate them later.
broker_suspend_member.body:
Suspending a member stops them signing in and taking part. It is reversible.

## Suspending

1. Open [Members](/broker/members) and find the member.
2. Press the three-dot menu on their row and choose **Suspend**.
3. Read the message and press **Suspend** to confirm.

The member gets a notification. Write a note on their record explaining why, so other brokers understand.

## Suspending several members

Tick the box next to each person and press **Suspend selected**.

## Reactivating

1. Press the **Suspended** tab.
2. Press the three-dot menu on the member's row and choose **Reactivate**.

The member can sign in again and is told their account is active. Press **Reactivate** only once: each press sends them another message.

## Limits

- You can only suspend and reactivate ordinary members. You cannot change another broker's or an admin's account.
- If an admin banned a member, only an admin can reactivate them.

> Suspension is a serious step. For a safeguarding concern, follow your community's safeguarding process first. You may only need to turn off the member's messaging, which you can do from **User Monitoring**.

broker_account_help.title: Helping a member who cannot get into their account
broker_account_help.summary: Resend a verification email, send a password reset, or reset two-factor sign-in for a member.
broker_account_help.body:
Many requests for help are about signing in. You can fix most of them from the member's record.

1. Open [Members](/broker/members).
2. Press the three-dot menu on the member's row and choose **View details**.
3. Open the **Actions** tab.

## "I never got the email to confirm my address"

Press **Resend verification**. Ask the member to check their spam or junk folder too.

## "I forgot my password"

Press **Send password reset**. The member gets an email with a link to choose a new password. You never see or set their password.

## "I lost the phone I use for two-factor sign-in"

Two-factor sign-in asks for a code from a phone app as well as a password.

1. First, make sure the person asking really is the account holder. Follow your community's process for this.
2. In the box above the button, write an incident reference and how you checked their identity. You need at least 10 characters.
3. Press **Reset 2FA**.

The member is signed out everywhere and told by email and notification. They can then sign in with their password and set up two-factor again.

> Before a reset, the app asks you for a code from your own authenticator app, unless you entered one in the last few minutes.

broker_adjust_balance.title: How do I correct a member's time balance?
broker_adjust_balance.summary: Add or remove hours from a member's balance, with a reason the member can see.
broker_adjust_balance.body:
You can add hours to a member's balance or take hours away. Use this to correct a mistake, not as a normal way to pay someone.

1. Open [Members](/broker/members).
2. Press the three-dot menu on the member's row and choose **View details**.
3. Open the **Actions** tab and press **Adjust balance**.
4. In **Amount (hours)**, type a positive number to add hours, or a negative number to remove hours. For example, type 2 to add two hours or -1.5 to remove one and a half.
5. In **Reason**, explain why. This is required.
6. Press **Apply adjustment**.

## What the member sees

The adjustment appears in the member's wallet as a separate entry. It shows your reason and "Admin" as the other party. The member also gets a notification.

## Limits

- A balance cannot go below zero.
- You cannot adjust your own balance. Ask another broker or an admin.
- The change is recorded with your name, the reason and the balance before and after.

## Correcting an exchange

If hours were recorded wrongly in a completed exchange, the Broker Panel cannot undo that exchange. The only fix available to you is to adjust each member's balance separately. Agree the correction with both members first. Mention the exchange in each reason so the history makes sense.

> Adding hours creates new hours in your community. Follow your community's rules on when this is allowed.

broker_supporting_members.title: Supporting members who find technology hard
broker_supporting_members.summary: Practical ways to help members who struggle with the website, and what the site does not let you do for them.
broker_supporting_members.body:
Some members find websites confusing or stressful. You can make a big difference by being patient and practical.

## Ways to help

- Use the **Never logged in** and **Onboarding incomplete** tabs in [Members](/broker/members) to find people who may be stuck. Offer a phone call.
- Sit with the member, or talk them through each step on the phone. Let them press the buttons themselves where they can.
- Send a password reset or a verification email for them from their record.
- With their permission, correct small mistakes in their profile, such as a spelling error in their name.
- Suggest the accessible version of the site if your community offers one. It is simpler and works well with screen readers.
- Write a note on their record about what helps them, such as "prefers phone calls".

## What you cannot do for them

The Broker Panel does not let you post listings, send messages or record exchanges as if you were the member. Every action a member takes must come from their own account.

Never ask for a member's password, and never sign in as them.

## Family members and carers

A member can link their account with a family member or carer they trust. The member does this themselves from the **Linked** tab in their **Settings**. The linked person can then help in the ways the member agrees to. This is the member's choice. Brokers cannot set it up for them.

broker_exchanges.title: Exchanges and listings
broker_exchanges.summary: Approve exchanges that need a broker, deal with problems, and tag listings that need extra care.

broker_exchange_when_approval.title: When does an exchange need a broker's approval?
broker_exchange_when_approval.summary: Which exchanges wait for a broker, and what members see while they wait.
broker_exchange_when_approval.body:
An exchange is an agreement between two members to swap time. In some communities a broker must approve an exchange before it can go ahead.

## How it works

1. A member asks to swap time with another member, usually from a listing.
2. The other member accepts.
3. At that point the site checks whether a broker needs to approve it.
4. If so, the exchange waits in [Exchanges](/broker/exchanges) with the status **Pending Broker Approval**. Brokers and admins get a notification.

## What decides it

- **Safeguarding.** If either member chose a safeguarding option that needs broker approval, their exchanges always wait for a broker.
- **Your community's rules.** An admin can turn on **Broker approval required** in [Configuration](/broker/configuration). With only that setting on, every exchange waits for a broker.
- **Low-risk exchanges.** If an admin also turns on **Auto-approve low-risk exchanges**, most exchanges go ahead without a broker.

Even with auto-approve on, a broker is still needed when:

- the listing has a **High** or **Critical** risk tag
- the listing's risk tag says **Broker approval required**
- the hours are above **Max hours without approval**

## What members see

While they wait, both members see that the exchange is waiting for a broker. Nothing else happens until a broker approves or rejects it. Please deal with waiting exchanges promptly, because the members cannot start until you do.

broker_approve_exchange.title: How do I approve or reject an exchange?
broker_approve_exchange.summary: Check an exchange that is waiting for a broker, then approve it or reject it with a reason.
broker_approve_exchange.body:
Exchanges waiting for you appear under the **Pending** tab in **Exchanges**.

1. Open [Exchanges](/broker/exchanges). The counter **Pending broker review** shows how many are waiting.
2. Press the **Pending** tab.
3. Press the view button on a row to open the exchange. Check who the **Requester** and **Provider** are, the listing, and any **Risk Tag**.
4. Press **Approve** or **Reject**.

## Approving

Add a note in **Notes (optional)** if it helps, for example "Please meet in a public place for the first session". Press **Approve** to confirm.

Both members are told the exchange is approved and they can begin. Your note appears on their exchange page under **Broker Notes**.

## Rejecting

You must give a reason in **Reason (required)**. Press **Reject** to confirm.

The exchange is cancelled. Both members get a notification that includes your reason. Your reason also appears on their exchange page, under the heading **Broker Notes**. Both members can read it, so write it kindly and plainly.

## Things to know

- You cannot approve or reject an exchange you are part of. Another broker must do it.
- You cannot change the hours or add conditions when you approve. If something needs to change, reject it with a clear reason, or talk to the members before approving.

> Before you approve, it helps to look at both members' records and any safeguarding choices they made.

broker_exchange_list.title: Understanding the Exchanges list
broker_exchange_list.summary: What each tab and status means, and what the exchange detail page shows.
broker_exchange_list.body:
[Exchanges](/broker/exchanges) lists the exchanges in your community. Use the tabs to filter them:

- **All**: every exchange
- **Pending**: waiting for a broker's approval
- **Approved**: approved and ready to start
- **In Progress**: the members are doing the work
- **Completed**: finished and the hours have moved
- **Cancelled**: stopped, or rejected by a broker
- **Disputed**: the members disagree

Each row shows the two members, the listing, the status, the hours and the date. The hours appear once the members have confirmed them.

## The exchange page

Press the view button on a row to open the exchange. It shows:

- **Exchange progress**: where the exchange has got to
- the **Requester** (the member asking for help) and the **Provider** (the member giving time)
- any **Risk Tag** on the listing, and whether it needs **Broker approval required** or **Insurance required**
- **Broker Notes** from the broker who decided on it
- **History**: each step, such as **Request created**, **Provider confirmed hours** and **Requester confirmed hours**, with who did it and when

Press **Back to Exchanges** to return to the list.

broker_exchange_problems.title: What can I do when an exchange goes wrong?
broker_exchange_problems.summary: How disputes happen, what the Broker Panel can and cannot do about them, and how to correct mistakes.
broker_exchange_problems.body:
Sometimes members disagree about an exchange, or hours are recorded wrongly. Here is what to do.

## Disputed exchanges

An exchange becomes **Disputed** when:

- the two members confirm very different hours, or
- a member presses **Report a problem** on the exchange in the phone app, for example because the other person did not turn up. The website does not have this button.

The members are told a broker will review it. You can see these exchanges under the **Needs action** tab in [Exchanges](/broker/exchanges). While an exchange is disputed, no hours move.

## What to do

1. Open the exchange. It shows the hours agreed when it was requested, the hours each member says, and its **History**.
2. Contact both members. Listen to each side.
3. Decide what is fair, then choose one:
   - **Settle dispute**: choose the hours to pay and write what you decided and why. The hours must stay inside the range the page shows, which is set in Configuration. The time credits move straight away.
   - **Close with no hours**: use this when the work did not happen. The exchange is cancelled and no time credits move.
4. Both members can see your note, and both are told.
5. If the dispute is about behaviour or safety, also follow your community's safeguarding process.

You cannot settle an exchange you are part of, or one where a member is staff at or above your level. Ask an admin.

## A completed exchange with the wrong hours

Open the exchange and press **Reverse exchange**, then write why. Both members' balances go back to where they were before the exchange, and a correcting entry is recorded beside the original. If a member has already spent the credits, their balance can go below zero.

To record the right hours, the members can then make a new exchange.

> Keep corrections rare, fair and explained. Members can see each one and its reason.

broker_match_approvals.title: What is the Match Approvals page?
broker_match_approvals.summary: Match Approvals holds suggested matches that a broker must check before either member is told about them.
broker_match_approvals.body:
[Match Approvals](/broker/match-approvals) holds suggested matches between a member and a listing that need a broker's check first. Neither member is told about the match until a broker approves it.

## Which matches come here

A match comes here when either member:

- chose a safeguarding option with **Require coordinator approval** or **Restrict matching**, or
- is under monitoring.

All other matches are shown to members straight away. When nothing is waiting, the page shows **No matches waiting**.

Brokers, coordinators and admins get a notification when a match arrives. For one member, at most five new matches are sent at a time. The rest follow later.

## Approving or rejecting

- If you approve, both members are told. The member sees the listing among their matches, and the listing's owner is told who may get in touch.
- If you reject, you must give a reason. Neither member is told, because neither of them ever saw the match. The same match is not sent again.

Your decision and your name are recorded.

## The page itself

The page has the tabs **Pending**, **Approved**, **Rejected** and **All**, and counters such as **Pending Review**. You cannot act on a match you are part of.

> Agree with your safeguarding lead what to check before you approve a match.

broker_risk_tags.title: Tagging a listing that needs extra care
broker_risk_tags.summary: Risk tags mark listings to watch, and can require insurance or, in some set-ups, broker approval.
broker_risk_tags.body:
A risk tag marks a listing that needs extra care, for example work at height or help with money. The tag is on the listing, not on the member.

## Tagging a listing

1. Open [Risk Tags](/broker/risk-tags).
2. Press **Tag Listing**.
3. In **Search Listing**, type part of the listing title and choose it.
4. Choose a **Risk Level**: **Low**, **Medium**, **High** or **Critical**.
5. Choose a **Risk Category**, such as **Safeguarding**, **Financial**, **Health & Safety**, **Legal**, **Reputation** or **Potential Fraud**.
6. Add **Internal Notes** for other brokers if useful.
7. Turn on **Broker approval required** if exchanges for this listing should wait for a broker. See the limits below.
8. Turn on **Insurance required** if the member who posted the listing must have insurance on record.
9. Press **Create Tag**.

Brokers and admins are notified when a listing is tagged **High** or **Critical**.

## What a tag changes

- **Insurance required** always applies. No exchange on the listing can start until the member who posted it has a verified insurance certificate that has not expired.
- **Broker approval required**, and a **High** or **Critical** level, only change approval when an admin has turned on both **Broker approval required** and **Auto-approve low-risk exchanges** in Configuration. Otherwise every exchange already waits for a broker, or none does.
- If your community copies messages about high-risk listings, messages about **High** and **Critical** listings are copied to brokers.

## Changing or removing a tag

The tabs filter tags by level. Use the edit button on a row to change a tag and press **Update Tag**. Use the remove button to delete it.

broker_insurance.title: Recording insurance certificates
broker_insurance.summary: Add, check, verify or reject members' insurance records.
broker_insurance.body:
Some activities need insurance. [Insurance](/broker/insurance) keeps a record of members' insurance.

If an admin has turned on **Insurance tracking enabled**, members can add their own insurance details from the **Privacy** tab in their **Settings**. These arrive here for you to check. If it is off, members cannot add them, and you add certificates for them here.

## Adding a certificate for a member

1. Press **Add Certificate**.
2. Use **Search Member** to find the member.
3. Choose the **Insurance Type**, such as **Public Liability** or **Professional Indemnity**.
4. Fill in **Provider Name**, **Policy Number**, **Coverage Amount**, **Start Date** and **Expiry Date**.
5. Press **Add Certificate**.

## Checking a certificate

- Use the tabs to see **Pending**, **Submitted**, **Verified**, **Expiring Soon**, **Expired** and **Rejected** certificates.
- Press the view button to see the details. If a file is attached, press **View Certificate File**.
- Press the verify button when you have checked it.
- Press the reject button if it is not acceptable, and give a reason.
- Press the delete button to remove a record you added in error.

## Why it matters

If a listing's risk tag says **Insurance required**, the member who posted the listing needs a verified insurance certificate that has not expired. This is the member shown as **Provider** on the exchange. Without one, nobody can start an exchange on that listing. This check applies even when **Insurance tracking enabled** is off.

> Follow your community's rules on what counts as acceptable insurance. Do not collect more personal information than you need.

broker_safeguarding.title: Safeguarding
broker_safeguarding.summary: Members' safeguarding choices, message review, monitoring, vetting decisions and what to do when you are worried.

broker_safeguarding_overview.title: How safeguarding works in the Broker Panel
broker_safeguarding_overview.summary: An overview of the safeguarding tools brokers use, and how they fit together.
broker_safeguarding_overview.body:
Safeguarding means protecting members from harm, especially members who may be at risk. The Broker Panel gives you several tools for this. Each one has its own article.

- **Members' safeguarding choices.**  When they join, members are asked whether they consider themselves a vulnerable adult. Their choices can limit who contacts them or send their exchanges to a broker.
- **Coordinator help requests.** When a member cannot message someone who is protected, they can ask a coordinator to help. Brokers and admins get a notification.
- **Message review.** Some messages are copied to brokers to read, depending on your community's settings. You review them in **Messages**.
- **User monitoring.** You can place a member under monitoring, so their messages are copied to brokers. You can also turn off their messaging.
- **Vetting confirmations.**  You record whether your community has completed its safety checks on a member. Members who consider themselves vulnerable adults can be contacted only by coordinators and vetted members.
- **Safeguarding Options.** You can change the list of choices members see when they join.

## Your community's process comes first

These tools support your community's safeguarding process. They do not replace it. Your community should have a named safeguarding lead. Know who that person is and how to reach them.

> If someone is in immediate danger, contact the emergency services first. Then tell your safeguarding lead.

broker_member_safeguarding_choices.title: What happens when a member chooses a safeguarding option?
broker_member_safeguarding_choices.summary: Each safeguarding option can switch on protections. Here is what each one does.
broker_member_safeguarding_choices.body:
When members join, your community asks whether they consider themselves a vulnerable adult. Members who joined earlier may have chosen other options, such as needing a coordinator to arrange their exchanges. Each option can switch on one or more protections, called triggers.

## What each trigger does

- **Contact through a coordinator**: only coordinators can message this member directly, and the member can message only coordinators. Anyone else who tries is offered **Request coordinator help** instead. The member is also left out of suggested matches. Their messages are not copied to brokers.
- **Require coordinator approval**: any ordinary exchange this member takes part in waits for a broker's approval. Group exchanges have no approval step. Their suggested matches also wait in Match Approvals.
- **Vetted members only**: only coordinators and members with a confirmed vetting decision can contact this member, and the member can contact only them. Until vetting is recorded for someone, only coordinators can reach the member.
- **Restrict matching**: suggested matches involving this member wait in Match Approvals until a broker approves them. Neither member is told about a match before that.
- **Notify safeguarding staff**: brokers and admins get a notification when a member ticks the option while joining.

If a member ticks several options, all their triggers apply together. The vulnerable adult option switches on vetted contact, coordinator approval, restricted matching and a notification to safeguarding staff.

These limits apply to contact aimed at the member: messages, @mentions, time credits and exchanges. Groups and events they belong to work as normal.

## Changing their mind

Members can see and revoke their choices from the **Safeguarding & support** tab in their **Settings**. When they revoke a choice, brokers and admins are notified. Its protections stop unless another option they chose still applies them.

## Seeing members' choices

The **Support needs not yet seen** counter on the [Broker Dashboard](/broker) shows how many members told us they would like extra support and have not been marked as seen since they last answered. Press it to open [Members' support needs](/broker/safeguarding/support-needs), where you can read each member's answers and mark them as seen.

> Treat these choices as private. Only other brokers and admins should know about them. Never mention them to other members.

broker_safeguarding_options.title: Changing the safeguarding options members can choose
broker_safeguarding_options.summary: Add, edit or switch off the safeguarding options members see when they join.
broker_safeguarding_options.body:
[Safeguarding Options](/broker/safeguarding-options) is the list of choices members see when they join. Brokers and admins can change it.

The page shows **Active Options** that members can choose, and **Inactive Options** that have been switched off.

## Adding an option

1. Press **Add Option**.
2. Fill in **Option Key**. This is a short internal name with no spaces, such as needs_coordinator. Members do not see it.
3. Fill in **Display Label**. This is the sentence members tick, for example "I would like a coordinator to help arrange my exchanges".
4. Add **Description Help** to explain the option in plain words. Add a **Help URL** if your community has a page about it.
5. Choose the **Option Type**: **Checkbox** for a simple tick box, **Select** for a list of answers, or **Info** for text only.
6. Turn on **Required** only if every member must answer it.
7. Under **Behavioral Triggers**, turn on the protections this option should switch on.
8. Press **Create Option**.

To turn on **Vetted members only**, you also choose a **Required Vetting Type**. It must match the jurisdiction your admin chose. If no jurisdiction is chosen yet, the site will not save it.

## Offering an option to new members

Each option shows how many members chose it. Switch off **Offer to new members** to stop new members seeing it. Members who already chose it keep it, and its protections stay in place.

## Editing or switching off an option

- Press the edit button on an option, make your changes and press **Save Changes**.
- Press the switch-off button and confirm with **Deactivate**. Members can no longer choose it.

## Changes that are blocked

If members have chosen an option that protects them, you cannot:

- switch the option off
- turn off one of its protections
- change its **Required Vetting Type**

You will see an error instead. This keeps members' protections in place. You can still change the wording.

> Changing options affects vulnerable people. Agree changes with your safeguarding lead first. Keep the wording short, kind and clear.

broker_coordinator_help.title: When a member asks for coordinator help
broker_coordinator_help.summary: What to do when a member cannot message a protected member and asks a coordinator to help.
broker_coordinator_help.body:
Some members have asked not to be contacted directly. If another member tries to message them, the site stops the message. It offers a **Request coordinator help** button instead.

When the member presses it, brokers and admins get a notification and an email. It says something like "Coordinator help requested", with the name of the person asking and the person they want to reach.

## What to do

1. Read the notification. Note who is asking and who they want to contact.
2. Open the protected member's record in [Members](/broker/members). Read their notes.
3. Contact the protected member in the way your community's process sets out, for example by phone. Ask if they are happy to be put in touch.
4. If they agree, arrange the contact safely. For example, you could set up a first meeting with a broker present.
5. If they do not agree, tell the person who asked, kindly and without giving reasons.
6. Write a note on both members' records about what you did.

## Things to know

- The Broker Panel does not keep a list of these requests. The notification and email are your record, so act on them promptly.
- Pressing the notification opens the **Safeguarding** page. That page needs extra access and may look empty. Use **Members** to find the member instead.
- The protected member's safety comes first. Never share their contact details without their agreement.

Sometimes the protected member is the one asking. A member who considers themselves a vulnerable adult can contact only coordinators and vetted members. The notification says when this is the case. Check that the contact would be safe before you help arrange it.

> A member may also be blocked because the person they want to reach only accepts contact from vetted members. They may then ask for a vetting review, which you handle in **Vetting confirmations**.

broker_message_review.title: Why are messages copied to brokers?
broker_message_review.summary: Which messages are copied for review, what you can see, and what members are told.
broker_message_review.body:
Your community can copy some members' messages to brokers so you can check that people are safe. The message is still delivered normally. The copy goes to [Messages](/broker/messages) for review.

## Why a message is copied

Each copy shows a **Copy Reason**:

- **First Contact**: the first message between two members
- **New Member**: a message from someone who joined recently
- **High Risk Listing**: a message about a listing tagged high or critical risk
- **Flagged User**: a message to or from a member under monitoring
- **Random Sample**: a message chosen at random for spot checks

Which of these apply depends on the settings in [Configuration](/broker/configuration).

## What you can see

When you open a copied message, you see it together with the messages that came before it in the same conversation, up to the 50 most recent. Messages sent after it are not shown. Earlier messages appear even if they were not copied. For a group conversation, you see the group's earlier messages. A message the sender has changed is marked **edited**.

## What members are told

When message copying is switched on, members see a notice in their conversations. It says messages may be reviewed by a coordinator for safeguarding.

## Your responsibility

- Read only what you need to make a decision.
- Never share what you read, except with your safeguarding lead or when the law requires it.
- Opening a copied message is recorded, and so are your review decisions, with your name.

broker_review_message.title: How do I review a copied message?
broker_review_message.summary: Mark a message as reviewed, flag a concern, or approve and archive it.
broker_review_message.body:
Message copies waiting for review are under the **Unreviewed** tab in **Messages**. The red number on **Messages** in the menu shows how many are waiting.

1. Open [Messages](/broker/messages).
2. Press the **Unreviewed** tab.
3. Press the eye button on a row for a quick look, or open the message to see the conversation before it.
4. Choose what to do.

## Your choices

- **Mark Reviewed** (or **Review** in the list): you have read it and there is no concern. In the quick view you can add **Review Notes** first.
- **Flag**: you have a concern. Choose a **Severity** (**Info**, **Warning**, **Concern** or **Urgent**) and describe the concern in **Flag Reason**. A reason is required.
- **Approve & Archive**: on the message page, this saves a permanent, read-only copy of the record in the **Review Archive**. You can add **Decision Notes**. Once archived, the record cannot be changed.

## Tabs

- **Unreviewed**: waiting for a broker
- **Urgent**: flagged messages nobody has reviewed yet. Check these first.
- **Flagged**: messages a broker has flagged
- **Reviewed**: messages already reviewed
- **All**: everything

## When the sender edits a message

If the sender changes a message after it was copied, the copy is updated with the new wording. It goes back to **Unreviewed**, even if someone had already reviewed or archived it, so a broker reads the new version. Any archive record already made stays as it was. A flag on the copy stays in place.

## After you flag a message

Flagging records your concern. It does not stop the member or warn anyone by itself. Decide what else is needed. You might place the member under monitoring, turn off their messaging, or contact your safeguarding lead.

> Do not tell the member you have flagged their message unless your safeguarding lead agrees.

broker_review_archive.title: Using the Review Archive
broker_review_archive.summary: The Review Archive keeps permanent, read-only records of message reviews.
broker_review_archive.body:
The [Review Archive](/broker/archives) keeps a permanent record of message copies that a broker approved and archived. Records here cannot be edited.

## Finding a record

- Use the tabs: **All**, **Approved** or **Flagged**.
- Type in **Search archive...** to search.

Each row shows the sender, receiver, listing, **Copy Reason**, **Decision**, who decided and when.

## Opening a record

Press a row to open it. You see:

- **Target Message**: the message that was copied
- **Decision**: what was decided, by whom, and any **Decision Notes**
- **Conversation Snapshot**: the messages between the two members, saved at the moment the record was archived

A note at the top reminds you the record is preserved exactly as it was reviewed.

If the sender later edits the message, the archive record does not change. The updated copy goes back to **Unreviewed** in **Messages** for a new review.

## Why it matters

The archive shows what your community knew and when it acted. It can support a safeguarding investigation. It also shows that reviews happened.

> Records in the archive are kept. Message copies in **Messages** are different: once reviewed, unflagged copies are deleted after the number of days in **Archive retention (days)** in [Configuration](/broker/configuration). Flagged copies are kept longer.

broker_user_monitoring.title: Placing a member under monitoring
broker_user_monitoring.summary: Copy a member's messages to brokers for a set time, and turn off their messaging if needed.
broker_user_monitoring.body:
Monitoring copies every message a member sends or receives to brokers for review. Use it when you have a concern about a member.

## Adding a member

1. Open [User Monitoring](/broker/monitoring).
2. Press **Add User**.
3. In **Search User**, type a name or email and choose the member.
4. In **Reason**, explain why. This is required. Future brokers will read it.
5. Choose a **Duration**: 7, 14, 30, 60 or 90 days. Monitoring then ends by itself: copying stops, messaging is switched back on if you turned it off, and the member is told their restrictions have been lifted.
6. If the member should not send messages at all for now, turn on **Disable messaging while monitored**.
7. Press **Add User**.

## What happens

- The member gets a notification that their account is under review. If you turned off messaging, it says their messaging is restricted.
- Copies of their messages arrive in [Messages](/broker/messages) with the reason **Flagged User**. Brokers and admins get a notification for each copy.
- With messaging turned off, the member cannot send messages. They can still receive them.

## Changing or ending monitoring

- Press the edit button on the row to change the reason, duration or messaging setting, then press **Save Changes**.
- Press the remove button and confirm with **Remove** to end monitoring. The member is told their restrictions have been lifted.

The counter **Expiring within 7 days** shows who will come off monitoring soon.

> Monitoring is a serious step that affects a member's privacy. Keep it as short as possible, record why, and review it before it ends.

broker_vetting_confirm.title: How do I record a vetting decision?
broker_vetting_confirm.summary: Record that your community has completed its safety checks on a member, without storing any documents.
broker_vetting_confirm.body:
Vetting means the safety checks your community carries out before someone works with people who may be at risk. [Vetting confirmations](/broker/vetting) records your community's decision only. It never stores certificates or check results.

## Before you start

The **Safeguarding contact policy** box at the top shows your community's jurisdiction and the confirmation it needs. Only an admin can choose the jurisdiction, so it is marked **Admin only**. Until one is chosen, you cannot record decisions, and every page of the Broker Panel shows a notice saying so.

## Confirming a member

1. Find the member. Use the search box or the **Confirmation status** filter.
2. Press **Confirm attestation**. An attestation is a formal statement that the checks were done.
3. Under **Underlying certification scheme(s)**, choose the checks your community completed.
4. In **Certified scope**, describe exactly what the decision covers, for example "befriending adults".
5. Add **Private broker notes** if needed. Do not enter certificate numbers or check results.
6. Set **Community review due**. After this date the confirmation stops counting until someone renews it.
7. Fill in **Authority membership expiry** if the scheme has one.
8. Tick the box to confirm the checks were done.
9. Press **Confirm safeguarding certification**.

## Renewing

When a confirmation has expired, the button says **Renew confirmation**. Follow the same steps.

## Why it matters

Members who consider themselves vulnerable adults can be contacted only by coordinators and by members with a confirmed, in-date decision. Until you record vetting for someone, only coordinators can reach these members.

> Never ask a member to send you a vetting document through messages, and never upload one. The checks themselves stay in your community's own process, outside this site.

broker_vetting_revoke_review.title: Revoking a vetting decision or answering a review request
broker_vetting_revoke_review.summary: Withdraw a vetting confirmation, or close a member's request for a vetting review.
broker_vetting_revoke_review.body:
## Revoking a confirmation

Revoke a confirmation when it should no longer count, for example after a concern.

1. Open [Vetting confirmations](/broker/vetting) and find the member.
2. Press **Revoke attestation**.
3. Choose a **Revocation reason**: **Community decision withdrawn**, **Member requested a correction**, **Safeguarding policy changed** or **Recorded in error**.
4. Press **Revoke confirmation**.

The change applies straight away. The member can no longer contact protected members who only accept vetted contact.

## Review requests

A member can ask for a vetting review from the **Safeguarding & support** tab in their **Settings**. This often happens when they are blocked from contacting someone.
