admin_help_faqs.title: Writing your own Help Centre questions
admin_help_faqs.summary: Add questions and answers about your own community to the Help Centre that members read.
admin_help_faqs.body:
The Help Centre explains how the platform works. You can add questions and answers about your own community, such as opening times or local rules. Members see them in the [Help Centre](/help), as questions from your community.

## Adding a question

1. Open **Content** in the admin menu and press **Help FAQs**.
2. Press **Add FAQ**.
3. Write the **Question** as a member would ask it. For example: "How do I earn time credits?"
4. Write the **Answer** members will see.
5. Enter a **Category**, such as "Joining" or "Events". If you leave it empty, it goes under "General".
6. Use **Sort order** to set its position. Lower numbers come first.
7. Choose whether it is **Published** or a **Draft**.
8. Press **Create FAQ**.

Questions are grouped by category in the Help Centre.

## Changing or hiding a question

Use the actions on a question to edit it, then press **Save changes**. Use its publish switch to hide it without deleting it. Press **Delete FAQ** to remove it for good.

## Good to know

- Your original wording stays available. When community translation is enabled, members can translate the question, answer and category in [Help](/help). The public [FAQ](/faq) is a separate platform guide; editing community questions does not change it.
- Until you publish your own, members may see a few general questions provided with the platform.

> Look at the questions members ask you most often. Those make the best Help Centre entries.

admin_ai_docs.title: Teaching the AI assistant about your community
admin_ai_docs.summary: Edit the short documents the AI assistant reads when it answers members' questions.
admin_ai_docs.body:
If your community uses the AI assistant, it answers members' questions using a set of short documents. You can edit them to add your own rules and wording.

Open **Intelligence & Diagnostics** in the admin menu and press **AI Module Docs**.

## How it works

Each document has trigger keywords. When a member's question contains one of those words, the assistant reads that document before it answers. It uses up to four documents at a time.

## Adding a document

1. Press **New doc**.
2. Enter a **Title**.
3. Enter a **Module slug**, a short name using lowercase letters, numbers, dashes or underscores. You cannot change it later.
4. Under **Trigger keywords (comma-separated)**, list the words that should bring this document up.
5. Write the **Body** in plain language: what the feature does, how to use it and what is not possible.
6. Keep **Active** switched on.
7. Press **Create doc**.

To stop the assistant using a document, switch off **Active**. Inactive documents are never used.

## Starter documents

New communities receive a starter set of documents. Press **Seed defaults** to add any that are missing. Your own changes are not overwritten.

> The assistant can still make mistakes. Tell members to check important answers with your team.

admin_support_reports.title: Reviewing problems members report
admin_support_reports.summary: See the problem reports members send from the site and keep track of what happens to them.
admin_support_reports.body:
Members can press **Help & support** on the site to tell you something is not working. Their reports arrive on the **Support Reports** page. Each report shows what kind of request it is: a problem, a question, an account or sign-in problem, or a suggestion.

Open **Platform Operations** in the admin menu and press **Support Reports**. The number of open reports also appears at the top of the admin panel.

## Looking at a report

1. Filter the list by status if you want, such as **Open** or **Triaged**.
2. Press **Review** on a report.
3. Read what the member wrote and which page they were on.

## Keeping track

- Set the **Status**: **Open**, **Triaged**, **Resolved** or **Closed**.
- Choose an **Assignee** to look after it.
- Write **Triage notes** about what you found or did.
- Press **Save triage**.

## Passing it on

Some reports are about a fault in the platform itself. Press **Copy engineering handoff** to copy a summary, including technical details, and send it to the platform team.

> If a member reports a problem, let them know you have seen it. It helps people trust the service.

admin_communication.title: Newsletters and keeping in touch
admin_communication.summary: Send newsletters, manage subscribers and reach out to members who have gone quiet.

admin_newsletter_send.title: Sending a newsletter
admin_newsletter_send.summary: Write a newsletter, test it, and send it now or schedule it for later.
admin_newsletter_send.body:
Newsletters are emails you send to your members and subscribers. Open **Marketing** in the admin menu and press **Newsletters**.

## Writing a newsletter

1. Press **Create Newsletter**.
2. Under **Details**, write a **Subject Line** and **Preview Text**. Preview text is the short line people see before they open the email.
3. Write your content. You can press **Load Template** to start from a template.
4. Under **Target Audience**, choose who receives it: **All members**, **Members and subscribers**, **Subscribers only** or **Specific segment**.
5. Press **Create** to save it as a draft.

## Testing it

Press **Send Test**. A copy goes to your own email address. Check it on your phone and computer.

## Sending

- To send now, press **Send Now**. It shows how many people will receive it. Confirm with **Save and send**.
- To send later, set **Status** to **Scheduled** and choose a **Scheduled Date**. Then save.

## After sending

The newsletter list shows open and click rates. Press **Stats** for more detail. You can also **Duplicate** a newsletter to reuse it, or **Resend to Non Openers**.

> Once a newsletter is sent, it cannot be called back. Always send yourself a test first.

admin_newsletter_subscribers.title: Managing newsletter subscribers
admin_newsletter_subscribers.summary: Add, import, export and remove newsletter subscribers, and share your sign-up link.
admin_newsletter_subscribers.body:
Subscribers are the people who receive your newsletter. Open **Marketing** in the admin menu and press **Subscribers**.

## Adding people

- Press **Add Subscriber** to add one person by email.
- Press **Import CSV** to add many people from a spreadsheet file. It needs an email column.
- Press **Sync Now** under **Sync Platform Members**. This adds active, approved members who have chosen to receive newsletters.

## Sharing a sign-up link

Copy the **Public Subscribe Link** and share it, for example on posters or social media. People can use it to sign up themselves.

## Other tasks

- Press **Export CSV** to download your list.
- Press **Remove Subscriber** next to someone to take them off the list.

## Emails that do not arrive

Open **Bounces** under **Marketing** to see email addresses that could not be delivered. Check them and remove any that are wrong.

Setting up how emails are sent for your community is handled by the platform team.

> Only add people who have agreed to receive your newsletter. Everyone must be able to unsubscribe.

admin_inactive_members.title: Reaching out to inactive members
admin_inactive_members.summary: Find members who have gone quiet and send them a friendly reminder to come back.
admin_inactive_members.body:
The **Inactive members** page helps you find people who have stopped using your community, so you can check in with them.

Open **Analytics & Reporting** in the admin menu and press **Inactive Members**.

## Finding inactive members

1. Choose a **Days Threshold**, the number of days without activity.
2. Press **Run Detection**.
3. The list shows each member's last activity and last sign-in, grouped as at risk, inactive or dormant.

Press **Export CSV** to download the list.

## Sending a reminder

1. Tick the members you want to contact.
2. Press **Mark as Notified**.

> Pressing **Mark as Notified** sends each selected member a friendly email inviting them back to your community. It does not only record a note.

The **Notified** column then shows who has been sent a reminder, so you do not contact people twice.

A phone call or a personal message often works better than an email, especially for older members. Use the list to plan who to call.

admin_safeguarding.title: Safeguarding
admin_safeguarding.summary: Set up safeguarding for your community in the right order, so vulnerable members are protected and still reachable.

admin_safeguarding_setup.title: Setting up safeguarding for your community
admin_safeguarding_setup.summary: Choose your safeguarding policy package, then add the matching safeguarding questions for new members.
admin_safeguarding_setup.body:
Safeguarding helps protect members who may be vulnerable. Setting it up takes a few steps. Do them in this order.

## Step 1: choose your safeguarding jurisdiction

Only admins can do this.

1. Open the **Broker Panel** from the admin menu.
2. Press **Configuration**.
3. In the **Compliance & Safeguarding** section, under **Safeguarding jurisdiction**, choose the one that matches where your community operates.
4. Press **Save Changes**.

If none fits your community, choose **Custom jurisdiction**. Vetted-only contact is then not available. See "Making sure vetted-only contact works".

## Step 2: add the matching questions

1. In the admin menu, open **Platform Operations** and press **Onboarding Settings**.
2. In **Safeguarding Config**, choose the **Country Preset** for the same place as your jurisdiction.
3. Press **Apply Preset** and confirm. This replaces your current safeguarding options.

## Step 3: switch the step on

1. On the same page, under **Step Configuration**, switch on **Enabled** for the safeguarding step.
2. Write a short **Safeguarding Intro** in your own words if you want.
3. Press **Save Settings**.

## Step 4: check the options

Press **Manage Options** to review the questions. See "Choosing the safeguarding questions members see".

> Do not apply a country preset that does not match your jurisdiction. Members who consider themselves vulnerable adults could then be reachable only by coordinators.

admin_safeguarding_options.title: Choosing the safeguarding questions members see
admin_safeguarding_options.summary: Create and change the safeguarding options members can choose, and decide what each one does.
admin_safeguarding_options.body:
Safeguarding options are the choices members can make about their own safety, for example "I would like a coordinator to help with my exchanges".

Open the **Broker Panel** and press **Safeguarding Options**. You can also press **Manage Options** on the **Onboarding Settings** page.

## Adding an option

1. Press **Add Option**.
2. Enter an **Option Key**, a short unique name for your team.
3. Write the **Display Label** members will read.
4. Choose the **Option Type**: **Checkbox**, **Select** or **Info**.
5. Add **Description Help** to explain it, and a **Help URL** if you have one.
6. Switch on **Required** only if every member must answer it.
7. Under **Behavioral Triggers**, choose what happens when a member picks it.
8. Press **Create Option**.

## What the triggers do

- **Notify safeguarding staff**: your team is told when the option is chosen.
- **Require coordinator approval**: matches and exchanges involving the member wait for a coordinator to sign them off. Their messages are not copied.
- **Vetted members only**: only coordinators and members whose vetting your community has recorded can contact the member, and the member can contact only them. Groups the member belongs to work as normal.
- **Restrict matching**: matches involving the member are held on the Match Approvals page until a coordinator approves them. Neither member is told about a match before that.
- **Contact through a coordinator**: only coordinators can contact the member directly, and the member can contact only coordinators. Other members are offered a way to ask a coordinator instead. Messages are not copied. To copy a member's messages, a broker or admin must place them under monitoring in the Broker Panel.

For **Vetted members only**, you must also choose a **Required Vetting Type**. It must match your jurisdiction, or the option cannot be saved.

## Offering an option to new members

Each option shows how many members chose it. Switch off **Offer to new members** to stop new members seeing it. Members who already chose it keep it, and its protections stay in place.

## Removing an option

Press **Deactivate** and confirm. The option is no longer offered to members.

admin_vetted_contact.title: Making sure vetted-only contact works
admin_vetted_contact.summary: Check your setup so members who asked for vetted-only contact do not become impossible to reach.
admin_vetted_contact.body:
Members who consider themselves vulnerable adults can be contacted only by coordinators and by members whose vetting your community has recorded. Some members chose "only vetted members" before that question was retired, and are protected the same way. If your setup is incomplete, or nobody has vetting recorded, only coordinators can reach them.

Members cannot see whether your setup is complete. So it is important to check it.

## What must be in place

1. **A jurisdiction is chosen.** In the Broker Panel, open **Vetting confirmations**. The **Jurisdiction** must show a place, not "Safeguarding jurisdiction not configured". Until one is chosen, every page of the Broker Panel and the admin panel shows a notice saying so.
2. **The jurisdiction supports vetted contact.** If the page says "This jurisdiction does not yet have a supported contact-vetting policy", vetted-only contact cannot work. Deactivate any option that uses **Vetted members only**.
3. **The options match the jurisdiction.** Each **Vetted members only** option must require the same vetting type as your jurisdiction. Applying the matching **Country Preset** does this for you.
4. **Vetting is recorded.** Brokers record vetting for members who may contact vetted-only members. They do this in **Vetting confirmations** with **Confirm safeguarding certification**.

## Warning signs

If the **Vetting confirmations** page says "An administrator must select the safeguarding jurisdiction before confirmations can be recorded", step 1 is missing. Fix it straight away.

> Never upload certificates, certificate numbers or criminal record details. Record only your community's decision.

admin_wellbeing_alerts.title: Wellbeing alerts and contacts
admin_wellbeing_alerts.summary: Follow up volunteers who ask for someone to get in touch, and choose who is told first.
admin_wellbeing_alerts.body:
When a volunteer says they are low or struggling and lets someone get in touch, your community's team is told. Every such request, and every alert raised from a pattern in someone's volunteering, is on the **Wellbeing** page.

Open the [Wellbeing page](/admin/volunteering/wellbeing) from the Volunteering part of the admin menu. A bell or email about a volunteer opens their alert straight away.

## Working through an alert

1. Press **Open** on an alert.
2. Read why it was raised, and the check-ins the volunteer chose to share, with their notes.
3. Check who was told, and whether each message was delivered.
4. Get in touch with the volunteer, for example with the message link in the alert.
5. Write what you did under **Add a note**, then press **Save note**.
6. Press **Acknowledge** while you deal with it and **Resolve** when it is done. Press **Dismiss** if nothing needs doing.

Notes are permanent. They cannot be edited or deleted once saved, so write them as a record of what happened.

## Who is told

When a volunteer ticks the box to let someone get in touch, these are told, in this order:

- the wellbeing contacts you name, and any extra email address you add
- your community's safeguarding staff
- the organisations the volunteer gives time to: they are told how the volunteer feels, never the note
- the staff of the community above yours, if there is one
- your community's contact address, if nobody else could be told

Each volunteer's team is told at most once a day. Later check-ins within that day are added to the same alert.

## The nightly activity check

Every night the platform looks at volunteering activity, such as a sharp rise in hours, many shifts close together or a long gap, and raises an alert when the pattern may mean burnout. Staff get one bell when a new high or critical alert is raised. The **Wellbeing** page shows when the check last finished, and warns you if it has not finished for more than two days.

## Choosing who is told first

Only community administrators can change these settings.

1. On the **Wellbeing** page, go to **Who is told first, and the support box**.
2. Under **Wellbeing contacts**, add up to ten members.
3. If you like, fill in **Extra email address** with a shared safeguarding inbox.
4. Write your own **Support text** and **Support links**. Volunteers see them in the "If you need support now" box.
5. Press **Save wellbeing settings**.

> Switching the Wellbeing tab off in your community's volunteering settings stops check-ins, the nightly check and all wellbeing alerts.

admin_records.title: Privacy, records and data
admin_records.summary: Check what has happened in your community, see members' consent records and decide how long old records are kept.

admin_activity_log.title: Checking the Activity Log
admin_activity_log.summary: See who took important actions in your community, and when.
admin_activity_log.body:
The **Activity Log** is a record of actions taken in your community, newest first. Use it to check who changed something and when.

1. Open **Platform Operations** in the admin menu.
2. Press **Activity Log**.

Each row shows:

- **User**: the person who took the action, with their email address.
- **Action**: what they did, such as **Approve User**, **Delete Listing** or **Grant Credits**.
- **Description**: more detail, where it was recorded.
- **IP Address**: the internet address the action came from.
- **Date**: when it happened.

The log shows 20 entries at a time. Use the page numbers at the bottom to look further back. Press **Refresh** to load the newest entries.

## Narrowing the list

Type a name, action or word into **Filter activity...**. The filter only looks at the entries on the page you are viewing. To search older entries, move to that page first.

## What the log contains

The log records many admin actions, such as approving, suspending or deleting members, changing categories and removing content. It also records some things members do, such as confirming their email address or changing their cookie choices. It does not record everything that happens in your community.

> The log shows members' email addresses and internet addresses. Treat it as personal information and share it only with people who need it.

admin_gdpr_dashboard.title: Finding your way around the GDPR pages
admin_gdpr_dashboard.summary: Use the GDPR Dashboard to reach data requests, consent records and the GDPR audit log.
admin_gdpr_dashboard.body:
The **GDPR Dashboard** brings together the pages you use to handle members' personal data. GDPR is the data protection law many communities follow. The same pages help wherever you have similar duties.

1. Open **Enterprise** in the admin menu.
2. Press **GDPR Dashboard**.

## What you see first

- **Pending requests**: how many members' data requests are still waiting.
- A red warning if any request has waited more than 30 days. It reads, for example, "3 overdue requests need attention".
- **New request**: record a request that reached you by email, phone or letter.

## Where to go next

The cards at the bottom of the page open the other GDPR pages:

- **Data Requests**: see and work on members' requests. You can also go straight to [the requests page](/admin/enterprise/gdpr/requests).
- **Consent Records**: see what members have agreed to.
- **Link GDPR Audit Log**: see a record of actions taken on requests and consents.

Press **Refresh** to update the figures.

> Deal with the oldest requests first. Many data protection laws give you about a month to reply.

admin_consent_records.title: Seeing what members have agreed to
admin_consent_records.summary: Check members' consent records and how many people have agreed to each type of consent.
admin_consent_records.body:
When members agree to something, such as your terms or optional emails, the platform keeps a consent record. You can see these records but you cannot change them. Only the member can give or withdraw their own consent.

## Recent consent records

1. Open **Enterprise** in the admin menu and press **GDPR Dashboard**.
2. Press **Consent Records**.

The **GDPR Consents** page lists the most recent records. Each shows the **User**, the **Type** of consent, whether they **Consented** (**Yes** or **No**) and the **Date**.

## Consent by type

The [GDPR Consent Types](/admin/enterprise/gdpr/consent-types) page shows each type of consent members can give. For each one you see:

- whether it is **Required** or optional, and whether it is **Active**
- the **Consent rate**: the share of your members' records that say yes

Press **Users** on a consent type to see who has **Granted** or **Denied** it, with the date and internet address.

The list of consent types is the same for every community on the platform. The platform team looks after it, so you cannot add or change types yourself.

> You cannot change a member's consent for them. If a member asks you about their consent, record what they asked for on the **Data Requests** page.

admin_gdpr_audit_log.title: Using the GDPR Audit Log
admin_gdpr_audit_log.summary: See a record of actions taken on data requests, account erasures and consent changes.
admin_gdpr_audit_log.body:
The **GDPR Audit Log** records actions taken on members' personal data. It helps you show what was done, by whom and when.

1. Open **Enterprise** in the admin menu and press **GDPR Dashboard**.
2. Press **Link GDPR Audit Log**.

## What is recorded

- work on data requests, such as creating, assigning, adding a note or preparing an export
- accounts being erased
- members giving or withdrawing consent

Each row shows the **User**, **Action**, **Entity** (what the action was about), **Entity ID**, **IP address** and **Date**. The **User** column shows the admin who acted. It is empty when a member acted for themselves.

## Filtering

1. Choose an **Action** or **Entity**, or set dates in **From** and **To**.
2. Press **Apply**.
3. Press **Clear** to see everything again.

The **Action** and **Entity** lists fill in from the entries you have already loaded.

## Looking at one entry

Press **View details** on a row. The **Audit entry** window shows the **Admin user**, the **Timestamp**, and the **Old value** and **New value** where they were recorded.

> Entries stay in the log. You cannot edit or delete them from this page.

admin_data_retention.title: Setting how long records are kept
admin_data_retention.summary: Choose how long old logs and notifications are kept before the platform deletes them.
admin_data_retention.body:
Data retention means how long you keep information. On the **Data Retention** page you can tell the platform to delete some kinds of old records automatically. Keeping less data for less time is good practice.

1. Open **Platform Operations** in the admin menu.
2. Press **Data Retention**.

Under **Retention policies** you see one row for each kind of record, such as **Activity log**, **Admin audit log**, **Notifications** and **Email log**. There are also rows for volunteering records, such as **Volunteer mood check-ins** and **Safeguarding incidents**. These only matter if your community uses volunteering.

## Turning on a policy

1. Enter the number of days to keep that kind of record.
2. Press **Save**.
3. Turn on the switch at the end of the row.

You see **Retention policy saved** each time a change is stored. The switch saves straight away.

While a policy is off, those records are kept with no time limit.

## Minimum periods

You can choose between 30 and 3,650 days. Some records have a longer minimum. The **Activity log** must be kept for at least 365 days. The **Admin audit log** and **Safeguarding incidents** must be kept for at least 2,555 days, which is about seven years. **Volunteer wellbeing alerts** must be kept for at least 730 days. If you enter less, a message tells you the allowed range.

## Checking what was deleted

The platform deletes old records each night. **Recent disposal runs** lists each run, how many records were removed and whether it was **Completed**, **Partial** or **Failed**.

> Deleted records cannot be brought back. Check your organisation's own rules on keeping records before you turn a policy on.

admin_reports.title: Reports and analytics
admin_reports.summary: Understand how your community is doing and download figures for funders and partners.

admin_community_analytics.title: Seeing how your community is doing
admin_community_analytics.summary: Use Community Analytics to follow member growth, exchanges and the health of your community.
admin_community_analytics.body:
All the reporting pages are listed together under **Analytics & Reporting** in the admin menu.

## Community Analytics

Press **Community Analytics**. It shows graphs and figures for member growth, exchanges and community health.

Press **Export CSV** to download the figures as a spreadsheet file.

## Other pages in this group

- **Impact Report**: the social value of your community. See "Creating an impact report".
- **Member Reports** and **Hours Reports**: detailed lists you can download. See "Member and hours reports".
- **Inactive Members**: people who have gone quiet. See "Reaching out to inactive members".
- **User Report**: each member's time credit statement, if your community uses the wallet.

You may also see reports for features you use, such as groups or newsletters.

> Figures are only as good as the records behind them. Encourage members to record every exchange.

admin_member_hours_reports.title: Member and hours reports
admin_member_hours_reports.summary: See who is active, how members join and stay, and where hours are being exchanged.
admin_member_hours_reports.body:
Member and hours reports give you more detail than the dashboard. Both are under **Analytics & Reporting** in the admin menu.

## Member reports

Press **Member Reports**. The tabs show different views:

- **Active**: members who are taking part.
- **Registrations**: how many people joined over time.
- **Retention**: how many people stay active.
- **Engagement**: how members take part.
- **Top Contributors**: the members giving the most.
- **Least Active**: members who rarely take part.

**Export CSV** works on the **Active** and **Least Active** tabs. On **Active**, it downloads your full member list, not only the period on screen. On the other tabs the button is not available.

## Hours reports

If your community uses the wallet, press **Hours Reports**. The tabs are **By Category**, **By Member** and **Monthly Trend**. Press **Export CSV** to download what you see.

> Downloaded files contain members' personal details. Store them safely and delete them when you no longer need them.

admin_impact_report.title: Creating an impact report
admin_impact_report.summary: Show the social value of your community for funders and partners, and download it as CSV or PDF.
admin_impact_report.body:
The **Impact Report** turns your community's activity into figures you can share with funders, partners and your board.

Open **Analytics & Reporting** in the admin menu and press **Impact Report**.

## Choosing the period

Set the **Report Period** with a **From Date** and a **To Date**. Press **Refresh** to update the figures.

## Setting the value of an hour

The social value is worked out from the hours exchanged and a value for each hour.

1. Press **Configure**.
2. Enter the **Hour Value**, the money value you give one hour of help in your area.
3. Fill in any other figures you have, such as your **Total Investment**.
4. Press **Save Configuration**.

The report can also work out a social return on investment. It needs your total investment and at least one outcome with a money value. Until then, it tells you it is not configured.

## Downloading

Press **Export CSV** for a spreadsheet file, or **Export PDF** for a document you can print or attach to an email.

> Choose an hour value you can explain, for example a local living wage. Say in your report how you chose it.

admin_federation.title: Connecting with other communities
admin_federation.summary: Partner with other communities on the platform so your members can connect and exchange with theirs.

admin_federation_switch_on.title: Connecting with other communities
admin_federation_switch_on.summary: Switch on Federation so your community can partner with other communities on the same platform.
admin_federation_switch_on.body:
Federation lets your community partner with other communities on this platform. Members of partner communities can then find each other, message and exchange, depending on what you agree.

## Switching it on

1. Open [Module Configuration](/admin/module-configuration).
2. Find **Federation** and press its switch.

A new entry, **Partner Timebanks**, then appears under **Overview** in the admin menu. This is where you manage partnerships.

The platform team also controls whether communities on your installation can connect. If the partner directory stays empty, ask them.

## Members choose for themselves

Switching federation on does not share anyone automatically. Each member decides. They visit the federation page in the member menu and press **Enable Federation**. They can also choose how visible their profile is.

## Other platforms

Partnerships are only with communities on this platform. Connecting with other platforms is not available.

> Before you partner with another community, talk to them. Agree how you will handle problems between members.

admin_federation_partnerships.title: Requesting and managing partnerships
admin_federation_partnerships.summary: Ask another community to partner with yours, answer their requests and choose what members can share.
admin_federation_partnerships.body:
You manage partnerships in **Partner Timebanks**. Open it from **Overview** in the admin menu.

## Asking a community to partner

1. Press **Partner directory**, then the **Browse partners** tab.
2. Search for the community.
3. Press **Request Partnership**.
4. Add a short message if you like, then press **Send Request**.

The button changes to **Request Pending**. The other community can accept, decline or suggest different terms.

## Answering a request

1. Press **Partnerships**, then the **Incoming Requests** tab.
2. Press **Approve** or **Reject**.
3. Or press **Suggest different terms**. Choose the **Partnership level** and **What members can share**, then send it back.

## Changing what members can share

Open an active partnership and choose the **Permissions** tab. Change what members can share. You can only do this while the partnership is active.

## Ending a partnership

Open the partnership and press **Terminate**. Members of both communities lose access to each other's profiles, messages and exchanges.

## How your community appears to others

Press **Partner directory**, then **Our listing**. Check your community name, description, contact email, website and topics, then save your changes.
